Use a first-order custom JVP from exact-derived physical derivative polynomials to avoid cancellation introduced by differentiating rounded moving normalization anchors. Validate this rule independently and keep prepared model coefficients outside the differentiation contract. Numerical uncertainty near parameter boundaries or moving knots, unresolved cancellation, and unrepresentable intended derivatives must remain explicit. Valid exact models can have rejected numerical queries, including some smooth stationary points. Persistent identical event functions may be represented together. This strict parameter chart rejects conflicting event-order changes at its reference; that rejection does not establish that the physical volume is nondifferentiable.

Compute local target-position sensitivity only under its nonzero-slope, stable-branch conditions, including any supplied target derivative. Independent target verification remains necessary. Do not turn event sensitivities into a static TOI correction, or expose a general optimizer through this extension.

Validate parameter derivatives with analytic references and independently rebuilt CAD differences, and target positions with actual Common/Cut operations. Compare finite-profile proposals, first-order proposals and CAD-only search on identical translation paths and ranges. Count preparation, compilation, attempted observations and final validation; separate repeated-target reuse from cold cost. Mathematical correctness, model-scoped reachability and practical speed are separate claims.

docs.title: One supplied event-order boundary
docs.text:
Add a host evaluator for one dimensionless affine design parameter with fixed facet normals and translation velocity. The caller supplies an event-order exchange at theta=0 and a positive parameter_radius to seed regular charts at its negative and positive values. This radius is neither a tolerance nor the returned validity radius. Require the same affine event inventory, exactly one pair meeting inside the translation interval, and preservation of all non-event validity conditions. Reject other simultaneous exchanges, endpoint collisions and geometry changes outside these conditions.

The certified parameter interval has open outer endpoints and includes zero. Check both exact polynomial closures against the fixed-parameter geometry. Preserve the two labeled affine events; their order changes across zero. Return exact host values, joint one-sided directional responses, and signed left/right parameter derivatives. Equal scalar derivatives establish only the ordinary parameter derivative at fixed step. A generally nonlinear direction map is not a JVP. Existing strict JAX charts and local target-position sensitivities retain their contracts.

Host specialization on either side and at zero reuses the finite-profile and target-set APIs, including their numerical packing limits. This does not discover boundaries, build a parameter atlas, differentiate target selection, or certify separately imported CAD. Validate any applied edit independently.

docs.title: Bounded dimension-and-position search
docs.text:
Within that supplied boundary model, add a host query on a compact closed parameter interval strictly inside the open certificate. Minimize absolute change from an initial parameter while choosing a translation step whose represented overlap volume lies in a declared target band. This is a bounded experimental design task, not automatic event discovery or a generic optimizer.

Use exact polynomial bounds over every affine event strip to exclude parameter intervals. Combine a tensor Bernstein bound with a fixed-parameter maximum upper enclosure plus a bound on the physical parameter derivative. The latter avoids relying on translation bounds becoming tight under parameter-only subdivision. No monotonicity or ordinary derivative of the maximum is assumed.

Return an independently checked binary64 parameter/step witness separately from a lower bound on the required design change and the resulting objective gap. Only a strict volume upper bound below the allowed band proves infeasibility. Resource exhaustion, unresolved extrema, packing failures and isolated feasible points can leave the search unresolved. A tolerance-qualified edit is not a claim of exact target reachability. Validate actual CAD independently and compare against complete fixed-profile rebuilding and CAD-only search, charging setup and final validation. A certificate is not evidence of a runtime advantage.

docs.title: Automatic continuation from a regular design
docs.text:
For the same one-parameter, fixed-normal affine family, accept a finite closed parameter window and an ordinary seed parameter. Discover the next exact root of the local validity guards in either direction, instead of requiring the caller to supply an exchange position and reference radius. Only an isolated exchange of two interior translation events is supported. Collect all guards vanishing at the root; a non-event condition, simultaneous exchange, changed event inventory, or failed adjacent-chart construction leaves that frontier unconfirmed. Failure of a sufficient certificate is not geometric invalidity.

Choose trial centers using exact distances and bounded refinement. Rebase the original affine family without rounding its vertices, and compare both chart closures with an independently rebuilt fixed-parameter profile from exact planes. Retain regular open chart intervals, certified boundary points, and the uncovered part of the requested window separately. A nonregular seed or an event at a requested outer endpoint can remain unresolved. Chart and trial budgets do not imply that the resulting coverage is complete.

Reuse the bounded design query with one global interval budget. Every uncovered interval or singleton contributes its distance from the initial design to the objective lower bound. Partial coverage may still establish the requested gap if every unconfirmed region is too far away to improve the witness. It cannot establish whole-window infeasibility. Recheck numerical witnesses in the original global parameter coordinate, including after non-dyadic rebasing.

Exact volume and feasible-design laws do not imply that the chosen sufficient certificates are frame invariant: selecting a separating axis can change the confirmed region after a coordinate transformation. Report that limitation separately from physical value accuracy. There is no selection derivative, general parameter atlas, automatic STEP decomposition, or simultaneous-event solver. Validate edits against actual CAD, and distinguish preparation, first accuracy-qualified action, and final certificate costs in comparisons.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
The experiment can evaluate volume through a contact without freezing a mesh topology. It is neither a general Boolean engine nor an extension of the imported-hole editing contract. Interior hole-center motion still has zero volume derivative. Radius-driven inverse design can cross the first edge while using a volume objective with a valid nonzero derivative.

At exact tangency the boundary can pinch despite the scalar volume being C1. A failed mesh closure check there does not refute the volume derivative; it prevents claiming a regular solid mesh at that configuration. OCCT's absolute tolerance floor can also spoil scale covariance of remeshing.

Use local coordinates and x64 for sensitive comparisons. Extreme radius to plate ratios and nearly complete stock removal lose relative accuracy in floating point. Supported examples do not certify arbitrary aspect ratios, second derivatives, or topology-changing edits of general input CAD.

The planar extension handles a supplied patch or the stated convex-cell contact collection with positive thickness. Existing overlap, arbitrary decomposition of nonconvex STEP input, and curved contact patches remain outside its contract. A directional response is only first-order information: verify the chosen finite edit independently. Mixed tilt can create wedges below OCCT's resolution even when the continuous response is nonzero. Edge-only or point-only contact can also create finite overlap despite a zero first-order response.

Boundary shape calculus and exact derivatives of cut discretizations are established techniques; see Wegert et al. (2025) and Wegert et al. (2026). This implementation makes no novelty claim for those techniques. Its evidence concerns the stated bounded families, derivative consistency, and measured accuracy/cost. The cited cut-AD constructions assume stable cut topology; they do not directly prove the birth of overlap at opposing-face contact. Broader generalization requires a separate decision.

docs.title: ADR-0023: Validated dimension handles and certified inverse queries
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Imported STEP solids carry no modeling history. ADR-0021 turns recognized through-hole radii and centers into differentiable parameters with validated OCCT rebuilds. ADR-0022 establishes exact event-delimited volume polynomials, model-scoped unreachability proofs and certified minimal-change search, but only for explicitly supplied convex cells. Its inputs do not come from imported parts: in the local fixture census, no imported production part was bounded by planar faces only, and cylindrical faces were the largest surface class.

The two lines answer complementary halves of one question: which dimensions of an imported part can change, and by how little, to meet a target, with evidence that the edited CAD matches. The following measurements, made on local NIST, FreeCAD and miscellaneous STEP fixtures, motivate a common layer:

  • After split cylindrical faces are unified, every recognized through-hole group rebuilds and passes validation (183 of 183). Preparing the mesh-based model, however, fails on 8 of 39 solids, or 14 after unification, because the reference mesh does not close at the weld tolerance. A discretized layer therefore needs a robust closed reference mesh first.
  • A planar face whose neighbors are perpendicular planes, or cylinders with axes along its normal, can be pushed or pulled by fusing or cutting the swept face prism. On the NIST and FreeCAD fixtures, such faces made up 22% of planar faces (279 of 1261).
  • In 164 of 198 sampled moves, whole-solid volume changed exactly by area times distance.
  • None of the remaining 34 moves met other geometry. Fifteen faces had inner loops whose bounding surfaces vary along the move. Sixteen showed a distance-independent volume error introduced by the Boolean result simplification. Three Booleans were invalid even for a tiny move.
  • Fillet neighbors were the most common reason a planar face was not of this kind (599 faces had no other reason).
  • OCCT's per-face offset (BRepOffset_MakeOffset with SetOffsetOnFace) produced a valid first-order result in 1 of 96 trials and is not a usable rebuild path for this purpose.
  • Some manufacturability distances are exact functions of these handles, checked against OCCT distances on rebuilt parts:
  • wall thickness between opposing parallel planar faces;
  • the ligament from a through-hole to a planar wall parallel to its axis, l0 - (r - r0) - s . n;
  • the ligament between two parallel holes.

Each law holds only while the pair remains the closest features: 79% of naively enumerated hole-to-wall pairs were separated by other geometry. The smallest wall thickness of the whole part came from such a pair in 6 of 36 solids and in none of the 16 NIST parts. There, it came from planes meeting at an angle or from tangencies.

Direct-modeling research expresses push/pull as a Boolean with the swept volume so that the result remains a valid solid, and notes that the motions of neighboring faces have no explicit expressions (Zou and Feng). Algorithmic differentiation has been applied to OCCT for parametrized CAD models (Banović 2019). The sources reviewed for this decision did not differentiate dimensions of history-free imported B-Rep. The DFM tools reviewed check rules and thresholds rather than computing sensitivities or minimal changes. This reflects the reviewed sources, not a novelty claim.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Introduce dimension handles: typed host records describing one editable dimension of a prepared, history-free solid. A handle names its kind, its faces in the prepared working solid, a reference value, and an admissible closed interval. Within that interval the face topology is unchanged and the handle has an exact volume and first-moment law. The initial kinds are:

  • through-hole radius and transverse center shift (ADR-0021);
  • planar face offset along its outward normal, for faces whose neighbors remain unchanged surfaces extended or trimmed by the move.

Further kinds, such as blind drilled holes, countersinks, counterbores and drafted or filleted neighbors, are admitted only after their exact law, interval derivation, and rebuild validation have been measured on imported fixtures.

Interval ends are events: the first parameter value at which the moved region meets other geometry or the edit changes topology. Hosts derive them conservatively from geometry before any edit. Beyond an event, a handle is unsupported rather than extrapolated.

Responses have two tiers, which stay distinct in API, documentation and evidence:

  • exact laws: volume and first moment as polynomials in the handle values inside their intervals, evaluated in exact rational arithmetic on the host and in float64 under JAX;
  • discretized responses: surface area, inertia and per-face manufacturability metrics evaluated on a frozen reference mesh moved by handle displacement fields. Their derivatives are derivatives of that discretization.

Exact constraints are local: wall thickness between two declared parallel faces, and ligaments from a declared hole to a declared wall or another declared hole. Each holds only after a geometric check confirms that the pair overlaps in projection and that no other face lies between them. A part-wide minimum of a manufacturability metric is a discretized response, not an exact constraint.

Inverse queries minimize a weighted change of handle values subject to target bands on responses. With exact-law constraints only, a query returns an exactly rechecked witness, or a proof that no handle values inside the supplied box satisfy the band, or an explicitly unresolved region, reusing the bound-and-exclude approach of ADR-0022. Bounds that support a proof are computed in exact rational arithmetic; floating-point Bernstein coefficients can violate inclusion (Garloff, Smith and Jansson). With discretized constraints, the query is a local gradient-based search with no certificate; its result must be validated after rebuilding.

Rebuild each edit in OCCT with local Boolean operations: fill and re-cut for holes, fuse or cut a swept face prism for planar offsets. Validate the rebuild through the removed and added difference regions, as ADR-0021 does. Their net volume and first moment must match the exact laws within the CAD tolerance allowance, and each region must lie beside its handle's swept region. A certificate applies to the represented handle model; only a validated rebuild connects it to the edited CAD.

Keep host preparation, interval derivation, rebuilding and validation behind the OCCT boundary. Keep evaluators array-based and JAX-transformable. The layer stays experimental. The existing hole-editing API remains supported while it is expressed through handles. Planar offsets and the inverse query follow in separate changes, each gated by an imported-fixture census. The census counts recognized, validated, wrongly accepted and unsupported candidates against an independent oracle.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Callers can ask minimal-change questions about imported parts, for example reducing mass within bounds on selected dimensions. They receive either a rechecked and rebuilt edit or a model-scoped infeasibility proof. Gradients of discretized metrics remain available to downstream JAX computations.

Coverage is limited to handles whose laws and events are implemented. Most faces of the measured parts are not yet editable dimensions, and the fraction that is must be reported per fixture rather than assumed. Topology changes, interacting features, curved neighbors and general direct modeling remain outside this decision. Certificates do not extend to discretized metrics, to geometry outside the declared handles, or to CAD that has not been rebuilt and validated. No production dependency or new kernel is introduced.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
triangulate_shape tessellates each face with OCCT BRepMesh, then re-evaluates every triangle corner from that face's own JAX-native surface parameters, independently of its neighbors. A vertex on an edge shared by two faces therefore gets two numerically close but generally distinct copies: the triangle mesh is watertight as a surface covering (no missing faces, see ADR-0016) but not watertight at the index level (no single, shared vertex identity for a physically coincident point).

This absence of true index-level sharing blocks prepare_hole_edit's closed_mesh weld (ADR-0021), which instead reconstructs identity after the fact from a position-distance tolerance bucket. On the local NIST, FreeCAD and misc fixtures, that tolerance weld fails to close 8 of 39 solids, and succeeds only by discarding genuine topological information in favor of a tunable distance threshold that cannot distinguish a real gap from independent re-evaluation noise.

OCCT's own BRepMesh triangulation already shares bit-identical boundary nodes and curve parameters between a shared edge's two owning faces (Poly_PolygonOnTriangulation), including a periodic face's own seam (which OCCT represents as two distinct, oriented boundary occurrences of that one face) and a degenerate edge's collapsed pole or apex. A prototype that identifies shared vertices from this OCCT edge topology (union-find over Poly_PolygonOnTriangulation node correspondence, matched by the edge's own curve parameter) and evaluates each global vertex once closed most of the previously failing solids.

That prototype picked one of the two incident faces' evaluations as each shared vertex's representative, which silently gives d(vertex)/d(params) one-sided: the other incident face's shape-derivative contribution at that row is zero, biasing any future optimization that moves both adjacent surfaces, and on NIST FTC-07/STC-07 (and STC-10) picking the worse of the two sides inflated a since-fixed evaluator defect (see below) up to 46% relative area error with no signal that anything was wrong.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Add extract_watertight_topology (host-side OCCT meshing, edge-topology welding, and manifold validation) and evaluate_watertight_mesh (a pure JAX function of explicit per-face parameters), plus triangulate_shape_watertight as a convenience composition of the two. All are explicit opt-in additions; triangulate_shape's output, including its exact floating-point values, is unchanged.

  • Shared vertices are identified from OCCT edge topology, not a distance tolerance: a union-find over (face, local node) pairs, matched through each edge's own Poly_PolygonOnTriangulation node correspondence and its intrinsic curve parameter (not vertex position). Walking each face's own TopExp_Explorer (rather than the shape-level edge-to-face ancestor map) yields two oriented occurrences of a periodic face's seam edge, handled by the same matching code as an edge shared by two different faces. A degenerate edge (pole, apex) collapses every node any of its occurrences references into one vertex, further unioned across degenerate edges that share a topological vertex.
  • evaluate_watertight_mesh(topology, params_list) evaluates every incident face's own surface parameters at its own nodes, then averages in two levels: first each face's own nodes at a given vertex, then those per-face means across the vertex's distinct incident faces. The second level matters whenever a face touches a vertex through more than one of its own nodes, e.g. at the point where a periodic face's own seam meets a neighboring face: a flat mean over nodes would weight that vertex 2/3 toward the seamed face and 1/3 toward its neighbor; this keeps it an equal half each, so jax.grad distributes symmetrically per incident face rather than per node. Separating topology (host, static) from this evaluation (pure JAX) lets a caller differentiate, jit, or vmap a mesh metric with respect to specific per-face surface parameters (e.g. one face's B-spline control points) without repeating the OCCT work, analogous to the existing extract_mesh_topology/evaluate_mesh split for the non-welded mesh. B-spline degrees are shape-determining dispatch and cache keys, not differentiable data, so they stay concrete Python ints on WatertightTopology.face_records rather than inside params_list: a degree sitting in the traced pytree would become an unhashable tracer the first time it was used as a dict key.
  • WatertightMesh is a registered JAX pytree (an equinox.Module of arrays only -- vertices, faces, max_gap), so jit and vmap can return it, not just take it as an argument. Host metadata that triangulate_shape carries alongside its triangle array (surface_type, per-face triangle counts) is not array data, so it lives on WatertightTopology instead (face_records, n_triangles_per_face), not on WatertightMesh.
  • WatertightMesh.max_gap reports an upper bound on the largest disagreement between any two of a shared vertex's incident nodes (twice the largest distance from any individual node's raw evaluation to the vertex's final welded position; exact by the triangle inequality), computed directly from those raw evaluations rather than from the per-face means above. The two are deliberately different: the per-face mean used for vertices would otherwise silently absorb a disagreement between two nodes of the same face (e.g. both sides of a periodic face's own seam) into that face's own mean, reporting an exact zero gap even when editing one control point measurably moves one of those two nodes relative to the other. triangulate_shape_watertight's optional tolerance raises when this bound is exceeded, so a genuine evaluator disagreement is surfaced and can be rejected against the shape's own CAD tolerance instead of being silently absorbed into an averaged position.
  • Validation checks both that every edge is shared by exactly two consistently oriented triangles, and that every vertex's incident triangles form one closed fan (a vertex-link check): the edge check alone accepts two otherwise-disjoint fans -- e.g. two tetrahedra -- pinched together at one shared vertex with no shared edge between them, since every edge inside each fan is still paired exactly twice.
  • Returns an indexed (vertices, faces) pair (a WatertightMesh), not a (n, 3, 3) triangle-corner array: the index level is exactly what welding establishes, and vertices[faces] reproduces the existing triangle-corner layout for divergence_volume and the other mesh metrics.

triangulate_shape and the watertight path share their OCCT host-side extraction and batched JAX evaluation (both already existed as one combined function; the shared parts are now two private helpers). Eleven of the twelve .step fixtures tracked in this repository produce bit-identical triangulate_shape output before and after this refactor (checked once, manually); the twelfth, nurbs_revol.step, raises NotImplementedError in both versions (an unrelated, pre-existing unsupported-surface limitation). A standing test checks that triangulate_shape reproduces OCCT's own mesh triangle for triangle (located node coordinates, face orientation applied) on four representative fixtures. A recorded hash is not a portable reference, because OCCT's mesh itself differs between platforms: sample_sphere has 2996 triangles on macOS and 3000 on Linux.

An earlier spike reported several percent volume error on FTC-07, STC-07 and STC-10. Welding was not the cause. OCCT placed some B-spline mesh nodes slightly outside the knot domain, where bspline_basis returned a zero basis and moved them to the origin, in both triangulation modes; welding only spread each bad node to the neighboring face. bspline_basis now continues the end polynomial pieces outside the domain, as Geom_BSplineSurface::Value does. Re-measured on each of the 39 local fixture solids alone, against OCCT GProp of that solid at the default deflection: every mesh closes; the relative volume error is at most 1.4e-4 on the NIST parts (FTC-07 5.3e-6, STC-07 2.9e-6, STC-10 1.4e-4) and at most 6.3e-3 on the coarse analytic samples, where it is discretization error. max_gap bounds the raw disagreement between incident faces before averaging, not the error of the averaged mesh. It reaches 3.1e-2, 7.9e-3 and 6.2e-3 model units on those three parts and 0.11 on CTC-02, whose volume error is 2.1e-5; the source of these gaps has not been investigated.

triangulate_shape_watertight can replace the triangulate_shape + closed_mesh weld in prepare_hole_edit, but this decision does not wire it in. closed_mesh's position-based weld keeps whichever duplicate point it meets first, while watertight welding averages, so the swap changes prepare_hole_edit's vertex positions, volumes and gradients on every fixture, not only on the solids that previously failed to close. That numerical change to an experimental public contract belongs in a separate change with its own measurements.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Easier:

  • All 39 solids in the local NIST, FreeCAD and misc fixtures close under triangulate_shape_watertight. nurbs_saddle.step, a single open B-spline patch with a genuine free boundary, contains no solid.
  • A caller can differentiate, jit, or vmap a mesh metric with respect to specific per-face surface parameters (e.g. one face's B-spline control points) through evaluate_watertight_mesh, with a shape derivative that is symmetric across a shared boundary, matching the planned use this ADR's context describes for future per-face parameter edits.
  • An evaluator disagreement at a shared vertex is a reportable, rejectable number instead of a silent, one-sided pick.
  • A pinched (non-manifold) vertex is rejected, not just a mismatched edge.

Harder:

  • Three function entry points now extract and batch-evaluate per-face data (via shared private helpers); a future change to that extraction must keep all three call sites' contracts in mind.
  • triangulate_shape_watertight raises instead of returning a best-effort mesh when OCCT edge topology cannot resolve a shared vertex (a free boundary, a non-manifold edge, or an edge discretization with no stored curve parameters); callers that need a result for an open shell must use triangulate_shape instead.
  • prepare_hole_edit still relies on closed_mesh's tolerance weld and therefore keeps failing to close those same 8 fixtures until a dedicated, separately scoped change adopts triangulate_shape_watertight there.

docs.title: 3D Extension Evaluation Report
docs.text: Historical evaluation, not a current acceptance report. Counts and numbers below describe the original fixtures and have not been regenerated here. The current implementation contract qualifies analytical exactness on correct sampled classification and finite primitive formulas; it does not guarantee arbitrary-pair accuracy.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Historical verdict: PASS on the selected fixtures.

The 3D extension extends the concept proof to 3D with 8 primitive types, 3 Boolean operations, and a unified stratum dispatch architecture. Dispatch accepts heterogeneous primitive pairs, but that interface coverage is not a general accuracy result.

Gate Criterion Result 1a Bounded pair analytical exact PASS 1b Intersecting stratum precision PASS 2 Boolean operation coverage PASS 3 Primitive coverage PASS 4 Stratum generalization PASS 5 Design principle 3D inheritance PASS

docs.title: Gate 1a: Bounded Pair Analytical Exact
docs.text:
Criterion: Bounded primitive pairs achieve analytical exact gradient in disjoint and contained strata.

Result: PASS

Validated with Sphere-Sphere subtract at resolution=64:

stratum gradient error disjoint d/d(r_block) 50.265482 0.000000% disjoint d/d(r_hole) 0.000000 exact zero contained (A in B) 0.000000 exact zero contained (B in A) d/d(r_big) 50.265482 0.000000% contained (B in A) d/d(r_small) -1.130973 0.000000%

5 of 6 measurement points are machine-epsilon exact.

Enabled by per-primitive volume() method returning analytical formulas (4/3*pi*r^3 for Sphere, 2*pi^2*R*r^2 for Torus, etc.) and jax.grad applied to these formulas in the stratum dispatch backward pass.

docs.title: Gate 1b: Intersecting Stratum Precision
docs.text:
Criterion: Method (C) outperforms Method (A) in the intersecting stratum.

Result: PASS

dimension Method (C) error Method (A) error ratio 2D (res=128) 0.14% 0.89% 6.4x 3D (res=128) 0.22% not measured comparison unavailable

The selected 2D sweep reported approximately fourfold error reduction when resolution doubled (64/128/256/512). This does not establish a universal second-order rate, near-contact accuracy, or a 3D advantage over Method A.

docs.title: Gate 2: Boolean Operation Coverage
docs.text:
Criterion: union, subtract, and intersect operations all functional with stratum dispatch.

Result: PASS

All three operations use _boolean_measure_with_dispatch with operation-specific per-stratum gradient rules (12 cells: 3 ops x 4 strata). Each cell has a defined gradient formula documented in the source.

Tested with 39 Boolean tests across homogeneous and heterogeneous primitive pairs including Sphere+Cylinder, Sphere+Plane, Cylinder+Plane combinations.

docs.title: Gate 3: Primitive Coverage
docs.text:
Criterion: All spec primitives implemented with SDF, parameters, and volume.

Result: PASS

Primitive Bounded volume() SDF jit/vmap/grad tests Disk Yes pi*r^2 2D circle pass 6 Sphere Yes 4/3pir^3 3D sphere pass 8 Cylinder No inf infinite axis pass 9 FiniteCylinder Yes pir^2h capped axis pass 10 Plane No inf half-space pass 9 Cone No inf apex+angle pass 9 Torus Yes 2pi^2R*r^2 major+minor pass 10 Box Yes 8hxhy*hz axis-aligned pass 11

168 tests total, all passing.

docs.title: Gate 4: Stratum Generalization
docs.text:
Criterion: Stratum detection works for arbitrary primitive pairs without per-pair code.

Result: PASS

_detect_stratum_generic uses SDF evaluation on grid to classify disjoint/intersecting/contained(A-in-B)/contained(B-in-A) for any primitive pair. No parameter-dependent logic. New primitives get stratum dispatch automatically.

Validated with 6 heterogeneous pair tests (Sphere+Cylinder, Sphere+Plane, Cylinder+Plane) covering union, subtract, intersect, and gradient computation.

docs.title: Gate 5: Design Principle 3D Inheritance
docs.text:
Criterion: Concept proof Method (C) design principles are maintained in 3D.

Result: PASS

The concept proof established: stratum label dispatch in custom_vjp backward pass. The 3D extension preserves this in _boolean_measure_with_dispatch: - Forward: exact SDF Boolean + heaviside indicator on grid - Backward: stratum label from _detect_stratum_generic, per-stratum gradient dispatch - Disjoint/contained: analytical volume() via jax.grad - Intersecting: straight-through estimator with grid-adaptive beta

Key findings during the 3D extension: - Thin sigmoid applied uniformly is a Method (A) variant (discovered and corrected) - Heterogeneous PyTree pairs need independent jax.tree.map calls - Drilling operations (penetrating cylinders) are structurally always in the intersecting stratum

docs.title: Drilling Demonstration
docs.text:
Sphere - FiniteCylinder subtract with optimization convergence:

lr final hole radius volume error 0.001 0.753 1.40% 0.003 0.758 1.40%

The reported drilling configuration is intersecting (cylinder penetrates sphere), so analytical exactness does not apply. The separate 2D comparison does not establish a sixfold accuracy advantage for this drilling case.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: The original launch recommendation was based on these fixtures. It is not a current release gate or a proof of exactness in three quarters of parameter space. Use the current theory and numerical scope when interpreting these historical results.

docs.title: Concept Proof Evaluation: Historical Scope
docs.text: This records the interpretation of the original two-disk concept proof, not a current acceptance report. The former overall PASS depended on claims that the current implementation does not satisfy.

docs.title: Corrections to the Original Conclusions
docs.text:
Original conclusion Current assessment Method C is analytical to floating-point precision in every relation region Partial overlap uses a grid sigmoid STE; sampled relation detection can also fail near contact Internal disk tangency has a first-order area-gradient jump For positive unequal radii, ordinary internal and external tangency are both \(C^1\) Method C reaches radius error \(7\times10^{-6}\) and is 3000 times more precise Superseded by the maintained grid-based demo; not current evidence of accuracy or general superiority Smoothing plus Method C supplies a validated hybrid optimizer Manual switching is possible; the experimental optimizer is unimplemented TOI supplies exact cross-boundary gradient transfer Event-time sensitivity does not establish the proposed static correction CPU scaling identifies a hardware limit and establishes GPU expectations GPU throughput remains unassessed by those CPU measurements

The canonical mathematical and implementation scope is in Stratification Theory, with the rejected static correction in the TOI discussion.

docs.title: What the Maintained Demo Establishes
docs.text:
The Method-C demo reports radius errors \(1.31\times10^{-3}\) for Method C and \(2.12\times10^{-2}\) for Method A after 200 steps on one disk-union objective. Method A uses fixed \(k=\beta=0.1\); Method C has a hard sampled forward value.

These are reported results for that configuration, not newly measured here, universal error bounds, or a search over both methods' best settings. A smoothed objective can have a small residual while parameters remain biased relative to the analytical target. Grid error also limits Method C. Compare parameter error and an independent geometric objective, not only each method's own loss.

docs.title: Findings That Remain Useful
docs.text:
For disjoint disks, union area is independent of centers, so a zero center gradient is correct. Escaping the plateau requires additional exploration information. Smoothing is one choice, without a guarantee that its signal is large enough or points toward a desired solution.

Array-based custom-VJP dispatch can compose with batching in tested cases. That proves neither all higher-order/forward-mode AD contracts nor accuracy of the backward formula.

Safe intermediate values help avoid invalid derivatives from unselected branches. Their clipping thresholds must themselves enter near-contact accuracy analysis; see the JAX discussion.

Do not reuse the original gates as current proof of exact intersecting gradients, novelty, or optimization superiority.

docs.title: CSG Reconstruction Scope
docs.text: BRepAX reconstructs candidate CSG representations from supported B-Rep faces. This is implemented functionality, with limits that differ from the original proposal on this page. Reconstruction does not recover a unique modeling history or guarantee an exact representation of every input solid.

docs.title: Implemented paths
docs.text:
Path Behavior Scope reconstruct_stock_minus_features Recognizes a box stock and groups connected cylindrical feature faces using the adjacency graph. A restricted recognition heuristic, not a general feature recognizer; candidate output needs independent validation. reconstruct_csg_stump Samples primitive sign vectors, classifies representative points with OCCT point membership, and builds a union of intersection terms (DNF). Sampling can miss cells. Unsupported faces cause reconstruction to return None; successful reconstruction is not an accuracy certificate. group_stump_primitives and compact_stump Group recognized bounded primitives and simplify intersection terms. These operations do not establish equivalence to the source CAD or recover its original feature history.

Adjacency is used for feature grouping. The sampled DNF reconstruction does not implement the earlier proposal's adjacency-pruned search over a learned Boolean connection matrix.

docs.title: Differentiation boundary
docs.text:
OCCT extraction, point-membership classification, and CSG reconstruction run on the host. DifferentiableCSGStump exposes primitive parameters to JAX, but its intersection matrix and union mask are static. Its derivatives therefore do not differentiate the reconstruction process or optimize connection choices.

DifferentiableCSGStump.volume integrates a sigmoid indicator on a grid and has discretization and smoothing error. It does not use analytical stratum dispatch. Separate Boolean APIs, including selected cases in evaluate_stump_volume_stratum, use stratum-dispatched measures; see the API overview for their limits. A finite gradient or a small optimization loss does not by itself establish an accurate CAD volume or shape derivative.

Trimmed-face distances cannot simply replace half-space ingredients in a DNF. The attempted trim-aware composition failed on analytical and B-spline cases; ADR-0020 records the counterexample and current raw-primitive-SDF rule. Face-level trimming remains useful for standalone distance queries, but is not a demonstrated fallback for general solid reconstruction.

docs.title: Evidence and further development
docs.text:
The integration report records measurements on selected fixtures. It makes no claim that BRepAX is the first or only system combining B-Rep input, topology, and differentiable evaluation. The previous assertions on this page that no prior work used this combination were not supported by a systematic literature comparison and are withdrawn.

Useful extensions should be evaluated against concrete reconstruction and editing tasks: compare point membership and measures with the source CAD, check gradients against independent derivatives, and retain failures and unsupported inputs. Vary sampling and discretization before attributing an improvement to the reconstruction method. Claims about topology-changing edits need separate evidence beyond derivatives of a fixed CSG representation.

The earlier effort estimates, predicted success rates, and proposed learned connection matrix were planning assumptions, not measured results or the current implementation contract. A future novelty or comparative-performance claim would require a current source-backed literature review and a comparable evaluation; this page establishes neither.

docs.title: Design Thesis
docs.text: BRepAX investigates differentiable Boolean geometry alongside practical STEP/B-Rep evaluation. The research question is how local contact geometry and moving boundaries determine derivatives, and how to compute them without confusing a numerical surrogate with the intended CAD objective.

docs.title: What Is Implemented
docs.text:
Method Current computation Limitation A: smoothing Public 2D union API: smooth SDF composition and sigmoid measure integral Temperature, finite-domain, and discretization bias; public 3D dispatch is unimplemented B: TOI Unimplemented Event-time sensitivity alone does not define a static gradient correction C: relation dispatch Hard sampled forward value; primitive-volume derivatives or sigmoid STE backward Sampled relation detection and intersecting-gradient approximation Experimental circular cut Analytic disk/rectangle measure and boundary-flux first derivatives Perpendicular extruded cut; no general CAD reconstruction Experimental planar contact Positive one-sided volume response to a supplied rigid direction, including complete collections of opposing planar contacts Known patches or explicit convex-cell bodies with disjoint interiors; nonlinear in direction; finite edits require CAD validation Experimental polyhedral translation Event-delimited, piecewise-cubic overlap volume, target positions and volume-range enclosures along one prescribed translation Explicit represented convex cells; host preparation fixes geometry and direction; no rotation or arbitrary STEP certification Experimental design sensitivity Volume and event-position sensitivities for affine vertex families, plus local target-position sensitivity Fixed facet normals and translation velocity; one or two design controls in a conservative parameter region; first derivatives only inside numerically resolved open event intervals Experimental event boundary Exact host values and one-sided responses across one supplied event-order exchange One design parameter, fixed normals and velocity, one isolated pair of events; no JAX boundary gradient or automatic boundary discovery Experimental design search and continuation Discover isolated event-order exchanges from a regular design and search a bounded dimension/position domain with a checked edit and objective gap Explicit one-parameter fixed-normal families; unsupported frontiers and exhausted budgets remain unconfirmed; no source-CAD or selection-gradient guarantee

The stratification explanation defines the current contract and contact regularity. Exact primitive-volume derivatives in simple relations do not make Method C exact everywhere or solve moving intersection boundaries.

docs.title: Contact Geometry Is the Mathematical Question
docs.text:
Point, line, and face contact can have different orders of area/volume change. Smooth sphere contact has a continuous first volume derivative, while positive-area planar contact can have different one-sided derivatives. Internal versus external contact alone does not determine the order, and changing the objective from volume to surface area changes the answer.

Four implementation labels are not a proved Whitney stratification. Contact sets and degeneracies need explicit analysis. Contact dynamics also does not establish a mathematical isomorphism with static Boolean differentiation: a trajectory has flow and reset rules that a static volume does not. The TOI discussion separates these contracts and explains why the previous static correction was invalid.

Finite motion asks more than the initial directional response. For a prescribed translation, polyhedral intersection vertices move affinely between geometric events, and the volume is a polynomial of degree at most three on each interval. This exposes finite overlap from edge/point contact even when the initial rate is zero. For rotation, higher terms depend on the full trajectory: compensating a pivot to preserve the initial velocity field does not preserve the finite path. The finite-response derivation separates these contracts and their established mathematical background.

An affine design family makes the polynomial coefficients and event positions depend on dimensions as well as step. Within a valid region, this connects changing-boundary volume derivatives to the position needed to maintain a target removal volume. Root existence, selection among several positions, and local sensitivity are separate calculations. Zero slopes, event boundaries and event-order bifurcations require separate analysis and lie outside the supported local inverse-sensitivity contract.

A separate host boundary evaluator handles one prescribed exchange with adjacent exact polynomials and explicit one-sided responses; it does not extend that local inverse formula.

Automatic continuation can discover those isolated exchanges from a regular design and connect their certified regions to bounded design search. It retains unknown regions in the global optimality assessment. This removes manual boundary placement within the restricted family; it does not establish a complete stratification. Even a geometrically valid family can outlive a chosen sufficient certificate, and certificate coverage need not be frame invariant.

Practical selection must distinguish a wrong ranking of the supplied finite actions from a candidate set that cannot reach the target. A few actual CAD observations can check and refine proposals, but absence of an observed target bracket does not establish that a target is unreachable. Equal probe counts, preparation costs, independent finite edits, and retained failures are needed to evaluate an improvement.

docs.title: Three Distinct Numerical Questions
docs.text:
Question What must be distinguished Locally constant objective An exact zero derivative versus a deliberately nonlocal exploration signal Near-contact volume derivative Missed contact regions, smoothing, quadrature, and true one-sided behavior Moving CAD boundaries A frozen-mesh derivative versus derivatives of regenerated geometry, trims, and topology

Smoothing may help exploration, but guarantees neither a useful gradient everywhere nor convergence to an unsmoothed optimum. A hybrid schedule remains a proposal.

AD through a fixed discretization differentiates that discretization. Shape calculus motivates accounting for moving boundaries; it does not remove frozen trim or connectivity assumptions. Bounded through-hole editing deliberately preserves clearance: its conservative edit budget is not a demonstrated physical contact event or topology-changing Boolean derivative.

docs.title: Evidence and Related Ideas
docs.text:
Density projection, differentiable rendering, hybrid dynamics, and shape differentiation offer techniques with different objectives and assumptions. They do not establish universal convergence, a fixed bias direction, or uniqueness for BRepAX. For example, nvdiffrast antialiasing uses an approximate local pixel-coverage model; it is not an exact Boolean volume derivative.

Comparisons need independent geometric values and derivatives, matched initializations and budgets, and temperature/resolution sweeps. Check rigid-motion and unit-scaling laws for both values and gradients. Convergence on a selected fixture does not prove that gradient sign is always correct or that a frozen-mesh plateau has one universal cause. The historical concept proof identifies earlier conclusions that no longer describe the implementation.

docs.title: Hybrid Optimization Strategy
docs.text: Combining smoothing and relation-dispatched gradients is a research proposal, not an implemented optimizer. The experimental hybrid_optimize entry point always raises NotImplementedError. ADR-0011 records the decision to keep scheduling at the optimizer level.

docs.title: Why Combine Methods?
docs.text:
An exact static objective can be locally constant in a design direction. Moving disjoint disks without changing radii leaves union area unchanged. No exact local derivative supplies a nonzero translation signal there.

Smoothing changes the objective and may supply exploration information. Method C avoids some smoothing in simple relation regions but uses a grid STE in partial overlap. Switching to it does not imply exact refinement. See Stratification Theory for the implemented rules.

The proposed schedule uses smoothing for exploration and changes methods or resolution for refinement. Its usefulness depends on objective, geometry, initialization, and budget. Gradients can remain too small, cancel by symmetry, or lead to a different optimum.

docs.title: What Would Validate a Schedule?
docs.text:
Compare with each individual method under matched initializations and budgets, including temperature and resolution choices. Independently evaluate the final unsmoothed objective and constraints. Report failed starts, contact events, parameter error, and cost, not only smoothed loss.

The former 3000-times-precision claim does not describe the current implementation; see the historical evaluation. An analogy with rendering does not establish this schedule's effectiveness.

TOI cannot supply nonzero exact static derivatives on a true plateau. Using future contact requires a specified look-ahead objective, trajectory derivative, or surrogate. The TOI discussion separates the valid event-time calculation from the invalid former correction.

docs.title: JAX jnp.where Gradient Pitfall
docs.text: A recurring pattern in differentiable geometry code using JAX.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
jnp.where(cond, x, y) evaluates both x and y during forward and backward passes, then selects the result based on cond. During gradient computation, the gradient of the unselected branch is still computed and can produce NaN or Inf if that branch involves:

  • Division by zero (e.g., 1 / d where d = 0 in the unselected regime)
  • arccos at domain boundaries (arccos(1.0) has infinite gradient)
  • log(0) or sqrt(0) in unselected branches

The NaN propagates through the selected branch's gradient, corrupting the final result even though the forward pass returns the correct value.

docs.title: Example: Two-Disk Intersection Area
docs.text:
The analytical intersection area formula uses:

cos_alpha = (d**2 + r1**2 - r2**2) / (2 * d * r1)  # division by d
alpha = jnp.arccos(cos_alpha)                          # arccos at boundary
lens = r1**2 * (alpha - sin(2*alpha)/2) + ...
return jnp.where(disjoint, 0.0, jnp.where(contained, contained_area, lens))

When disks are disjoint (d >> r1 + r2), the forward pass correctly returns 0.0. But the backward pass computes d(lens)/d(r1) anyway, which involves d(arccos(clip(x)))/dx at x = 1.0 (infinite gradient), producing NaN.

docs.title: The Fix: Safe Primal Values
docs.text:
Replace potentially dangerous intermediate values with safe substitutes in branches that will be masked out:

safe_d = jnp.maximum(d, 1e-10)              # prevent division by zero
cos_alpha = jnp.clip(
    (safe_d**2 + r1**2 - r2**2) / (2 * safe_d * r1),
    -1.0 + eps, 1.0 - eps,                  # keep arccos away from domain boundary
)

The eps margin keeps arccos away from +/-1, and safe_d prevents division by zero. These safeguards can also modify the selected lens branch near tangency or at very small scales. They therefore change values and derivatives there; finiteness alone does not establish accuracy. The distance floor has length units, while the cosine margin is dimensionless. Near-contact checks need independent limits or stable formulas outside the clipping regime.

docs.title: Relation to Custom VJP
docs.text: Safe primals address invalid intermediate derivatives. A custom VJP permits a separately specified backward rule, but does not itself make that rule exact or prevent evaluation of unused expressions. BRepAX currently evaluates candidate gradients and selects with array operations; its intersecting rule is a grid STE. See ADR-0004 and the implementation contract.

docs.title: License Strategy
docs.text: BRepAX uses Apache License 2.0 for all original code, with a transitive dependency on OCCT (LGPL 2.1) via cadquery-ocp-novtk.

docs.title: Academic and Research Use
docs.text: No restrictions. LGPL permits unrestricted use for research, papers, and collaboration.

docs.title: Personal and Open-Source Use
docs.text: No restrictions. The dynamic linking exception of LGPL 2.1 applies; users can freely use BRepAX in their projects regardless of license.

docs.title: Commercial Internal Use
docs.text: No restrictions. Companies can use BRepAX internally without LGPL obligations (internal tools are not "distribution").

docs.title: Commercial Redistribution (Closed-Source)
docs.text: LGPL requires that users can replace the LGPL component. Since OCCT is dynamically linked via Python wheels, this is satisfied by default. Users can install a different version of cadquery-ocp-novtk without modifying BRepAX.

docs.title: Industry Precedent
docs.text: CadQuery (Apache 2.0) and build123d use the identical structure: Apache 2.0 wrapper around LGPL OCCT. Both have wide adoption in industry and academia without license issues.

docs.title: Evaluation on NIST MBE PMI Test Cases
Overview
docs.text:
BRepAX was evaluated on 28 public STEP files from three sources: the NIST MBE PMI test cases (16 files), the FreeCAD mechanical parts library (9 files), and OCCT/CadQuery test geometry (3 files). The evaluation covers face conversion, CSG reconstruction, and scalability.

Key results:

  • Face conversion: 4,080 / 4,080 = 100% (all surface types including rational B-splines)
  • CSG reconstruction: 24 / 24 tested files successful (up to 664 faces)
  • BSpline faces: 104 / 4,080 = 2.5% of faces in real parts are freeform NURBS

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
Source Files Description NIST FTC (Fully-Toleranced Test Cases) 6 FTC-06 through FTC-11: machined parts with holes, pockets, chamfers NIST CTC (Combined Test Cases) 5 CTC-01 through CTC-05: complex parts with GD&T NIST STC (Simplified Test Cases) 5 STC-06 through STC-10: simplified versions of FTC/CTC FreeCAD Library 9 Ball bearings, hex nuts (M3-M10), linear slide, GT2 pulley OCCT / CadQuery 3 Linkrods, screw, cube+cylinder test geometry

All files are public domain or open source and may be used without restriction.

Aggregate across all 28 files (4,080 faces):

97.5% of faces are analytical surfaces representable by the five classical primitive types. B-spline surfaces appear in 7 of 28 files, concentrated in parts with fillet blends and freeform features.
