sensitivity = jax.jit(polyhedral_parameter_position_sensitivity)(
    design.model, 23 / 32, theta,
)  # [1, -15/32]: fixed physical target, dimensionless design parameters.

An AffinePolyhedralCell has vertices (N, 3) and parameter displacements (P, N, 3). Its vertex map is affine in theta; vertices, displacement coefficients and velocity share a length unit. Preparation checks the fixed facet-normal assumption and derives sufficient strict linear conditions on theta. These preserve cell validity, disjoint interiors and event ordering; they need not describe the largest valid region. Conflicting event-order changes at the reference design are rejected even if volume itself is smooth.

polyhedral_parameter_volume supports jit, vmap and first-order JVP/reverse derivatives in step and design parameters inside resolved open intervals. Its custom JVP uses the physical derivative polynomials, avoiding cancellation from differentiating rounded moving normalization anchors. Prepared model coefficients are not differentiation variables; higher derivatives are outside the contract. It returns NaN near moving events or parameter boundaries and when value/derivative cancellation or numerical range is unresolved. This can include a mathematically smooth stationary point. That is a limitation of the numerical derivative chart, not a claim that physical volume is undefined. Host specialization checks exact parameter conditions and creates a complete fixed-parameter translation profile with the existing boundary-value, one-sided-slope and target-query contracts. Specialization evaluates the affine represented family; independently rounded new vertices or rebuilt CAD can differ from that model.

The position-sensitivity query computes the local volume-level-set derivative; it does not verify a target residual or select a root. Check the root first. Zero or unresolved slope, event boundaries and branch changes require separate treatment. Supply target_parameter_gradient when the target itself changes with the design. For fixed dimensionless parameters, scaling all lengths by s scales volume and its parameter derivatives by s**3; convert physical length sensitivities by the chain rule. Retain independent CAD validation.

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.parametric \
  --output /tmp/parametric.json

This benchmark compares finite-profile inversion, first-order proposals and CAD-only search on the same supplied translation paths and ranges. It checks root inventories and path-unreachable targets against independent prism sections, evaluates design sensitivities, and validates actual rebuilt CAD edits. Parameter-volume differences rebuild CAD directly; position differences use specialized roots checked against independent section solutions and rebuilt CAD residuals. Failures and unsupported cases remain in the results. Timings include preparation and attempted CAD operations, but share one process and JAX caches; they are diagnostics rather than isolated cold-start comparisons.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.polyhedral_parameter
docs.text:
Local design sensitivities for fixed-normal polyhedral translation paths.

Host preparation certifies an open parameter region for represented vertex families. Within that region, JAX differentiates the changing volume rather than a frozen set of polynomial coefficients. Events and their ordering remain explicit; neither this chart nor its derivatives certify original CAD input.

docs.title: AffinePolyhedralCell dataclass
docs.text:
Bounded convex cell with affine vertex displacements.

vertices has shape (N, 3); parameter_displacements has shape (P, N, 3), with P equal to one or two. At dimensionless parameters theta, vertex i is vertices[i] + sum(theta[p] * displacements[p, i]). Vertices and displacements use the same length unit. Preparation checks fixed facet normals and derives a conservative open validity region.

docs.title: PolyhedralParameterModel
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Packed changing-volume chart, evaluated only inside resolved chambers.

Prepare on the host with :func:prepare_polyhedral_parameter. Floating event positions are rounded values, not exact contact classifications. Strict guards with roundoff bands reject uncertain parameter/chamber boundaries; use host specialization for exact model event diagnostics.

docs.title: ParameterTranslationEvent dataclass
docs.text:
Affine combinatorial event; not necessarily a physical contact event.

Its exact step is reference_step + parameter_gradient dot theta. The derivative is valid only in the prepared open parameter region.

docs.title: PreparedPolyhedralParameter dataclass
docs.text:
Exact parameter certificates and their conservative numerical evaluator.

Each parameter_constraints row is (constant, parameter coefficients) and must be strictly positive. These sufficient conditions need not be the largest valid region. The reference is theta=0. Event-order ties with different affine expressions are unsupported, even if volume is smooth.

docs.title: prepare_polyhedral_parameter(fixed_cells, moving_cells, velocity, *, max_step)
docs.text:
Prepare a local design chart for a specified finite translation.

Each cell is a bounded, positive-volume vertex hull. Parameters are dimensionless and reference theta=0; there must be one or two shared parameters. Vertex displacements must preserve facet normals exactly for the represented inputs. Same-body interiors and initial cross-body interiors remain disjoint under the returned linear validity conditions. A nonregular reference, including an event tie that splits with theta, raises ValueError. This rejects some otherwise valid volume families.

The moving body follows vertex(theta) + step * velocity for 0 <= step <= max_step. Step is dimensionless; velocity uses the vertex length unit. Geometry and velocity are host inputs; t and theta are the differentiation variables. Preparation enumerates plane triples and is intended for small cells. No CAD observations are fitted.

First JAX derivatives are supported in strict, numerically resolved open chambers. Values at or near a changing event are NaN in that evaluator; specialize on the host for a complete fixed-parameter profile and one-sided slopes. A custom JVP uses exact-derived physical derivative polynomials to avoid cancellation in the moving normalization's floating chain rule. Prepared model arrays are explicitly frozen; only step and theta are differentiated. This separates discrete chart selection from changing-geometry evaluation. Neither an uncertain floating guard nor a source-CAD contact is certified.

Exact global rigid frame changes preserve values and step/parameter derivatives. Scaling vertices, displacements and velocity by s scales all those quantities by s**3, keeping dimensionless theta and step fixed. Independently rounded transformed inputs can change validity or reject. A derivative with respect to a physical length parameter instead has the corresponding chain-rule units.

Example::

from itertools import product
import jax
import numpy as np

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
box = np.array(list(product((0., 1.), repeat=3)))
fixed = AffinePolyhedralCell(box, np.zeros((1, 8, 3)))
shift = np.tile(np.array([1., 0., 0.]), (1, 8, 1))
moving = AffinePolyhedralCell(box + (2., 0., 0.), shift)
prepared = prepare_polyhedral_parameter(
    [fixed], [moving], (-1., 0., 0.), max_step=4.
)
# Initial gap grows by theta; the interior overlap is step - 1 - theta.
volume = polyhedral_parameter_volume(prepared.model, 1.5, np.array([0.1]))

docs.title: specialize_polyhedral_parameter(prepared, parameters)
docs.text:
Substitute theta exactly, yielding an ordinary finite translation profile.

Supplied finite float64 theta values are interpreted as exact rationals. Strict validity guards are checked on the host; invalid parameters raise ValueError. This uses the prepared affine family, not newly rounded vertex coordinates. Existing profile packing may reject unresolved events or underflow. The result supports the usual value, slope and target queries.

docs.title: polyhedral_parameter_volume(model, step, parameters)
docs.text:
Evaluate volume with live step and design parameters in an open chamber.

Supports jit, vmap and first JVP/reverse derivatives in step and theta. A custom JVP evaluates exact-derived derivatives of the same volume; it avoids cancellation in a floating moving-origin chain rule. Model arrays are frozen, and higher derivatives are outside the contract. Strict linear guards and conservative roundoff bands reject uncertain classification. At/near events, outside the parameter region or step interval, or when a required nonzero value/derivative monomial underflows, or cancellation prevents resolving a value/derivative sum, value and intended derivatives are NaN. This includes some valid interior stationary points. Subnormal query inputs also reject because XLA may flush them before arithmetic. Packing/evaluation is floating arithmetic, not an exact volume oracle. Use :func:specialize_polyhedral_parameter for boundary values and slopes.

docs.title: polyhedral_parameter_events(model, parameters)
docs.text:
Return rounded affine knots, including zero and max_step.

Supports jit/vmap and parameter AD inside the resolved parameter region. These rounded positions are not exact event classifications. Invalid or roundoff-ambiguous parameters return NaNs; host specialization retains the exact rational event positions. Some knots may be combinatorial only.

docs.title: polyhedral_parameter_position_sensitivity(model, step, parameters, *, target_parameter_gradient=None)
docs.text:
Differentiate a local volume level set through the supplied position.

Returns (target_parameter_gradient - dV/dtheta) / (dV/dstep). The default holds the physical volume target fixed; an explicit target gradient uses volume per dimensionless parameter. This is not a root finder or a check that step attains a requested target. Verify the root residual separately. The selected root branch must be simple and inside a resolved chamber. Invalid queries, unresolved/zero slopes, and underflow of a nonzero target difference or resulting ratio return NaNs. Equal represented target and volume derivatives retain zero sensitivity. No derivative at extrema, event boundaries or switching between root branches is promised.

docs.title: One supplied event-order boundary
docs.text:
brepax.experimental.polyhedral_boundary handles one supplied exchange at theta=0 for a single affine design parameter. It requires fixed facet normals and translation velocity, valid bounded cells, disjoint same-body interiors, and no initial cross-body overlap throughout its certified region.

from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import product

import jax
import numpy as np

from brepax.experimental.polyhedral_boundary import (
    polyhedral_event_boundary_response,
    prepare_polyhedral_event_boundary,
    specialize_polyhedral_event_boundary,
)
from brepax.experimental.polyhedral_parameter import AffinePolyhedralCell
from brepax.experimental.polyhedral_targets import polyhedral_translation_targets

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
stock = np.array(list(product((0.0, 1.0), repeat=3)))
tool = np.array(list(product((-1.5, -0.5), (-1.0, 2.0), (-1.0, 2.0))))
changes = np.zeros((1, 8, 3))
changes[0, tool[:, 0] == -1.5, 0] = -1.0
boundary = prepare_polyhedral_event_boundary(
    [AffinePolyhedralCell(stock, np.zeros((1, 8, 3)))],
    [AffinePolyhedralCell(tool, changes)], (1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    max_step=3, parameter_radius=Fraction(1, 8),
)
response = polyhedral_event_boundary_response(boundary, Fraction(3, 2))
# Signed left/right theta derivatives are 1 and 0; no ordinary theta derivative.
path = specialize_polyhedral_event_boundary(boundary, Fraction(1, 8))
solutions = polyhedral_translation_targets(
    path, 1, step_tolerance=1e-12, volume_tolerance=1e-12,
)
# Full-volume solutions form the interval [3/2, 13/8].

parameter_radius selects reference points at -radius and +radius; it is not a tolerance, finite-difference step, or claimed validity bound. Inspect parameter_interval: its outer endpoints are open, zero is included, and None denotes an unbounded endpoint. Preparation rejects references that do not certify exactly one isolated pair of events with the same surrounding inventory. The returned events are stable affine labels, not chronological positions on both sides.

The response query evaluates (step, theta=0) along epsilon * (step_direction, parameter_direction) as epsilon decreases to zero from above. Results are exact Fraction values. The signed left parameter derivative is the negative of the response in direction (0,-1). ordinary_parameter_derivative returns their common value when they agree, or None otherwise; it is not a joint differentiability certificate. Directions exiting the supplied translation interval or inconsistent tangent limits reject.

Preparation and responses are host operations, without jit, vmap or boundary AD. Specialization requires JAX x64 and retains the existing profile packing/target-query limits. All queries preserve supplied Fraction scalars; float scalars denote their exact binary64 values. With dimensionless step and design parameter, scaling geometry, displacement coefficients and velocity by s > 0 scales volume and directional responses by s**3. Exact rigid coordinate changes preserve them; independently rounded inputs can change the certificate. See the directional derivation.

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.event_boundary \
  --output /tmp/event-boundary.json

For each supplied design dimension, this bounded comparison finds a target position along a prescribed translation path. It compares reuse of a boundary model, rebuilding the exact fixed-dimension profile, and CAD-only search at the same requested accuracy; it does not search for the smallest dimension change. Boolean operations use disposable copies of both inputs so repeated observations preserve source topology and tolerances; copying time is included in CAD cost. Exact target existence and meeting the CAD residual allowance are reported separately. Failed probes and model/source disagreements remain visible even when a selected edit passes its final CAD checks.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.polyhedral_boundary
docs.text: Host queries across one supplied polyhedral event-order boundary.

docs.title: PreparedPolyhedralEventBoundary dataclass
docs.text:
Exact host certificate for an exchange supplied at theta=0.

parameter_interval is open at each finite outer endpoint and includes zero. None denotes an unbounded endpoint. events labels the two affine event functions; their tuple order is not chronological on both sides. No original-CAD contact or rounded transformed input is certified.

docs.title: PolyhedralBoundaryResponse dataclass
docs.text:
Exact volume and first responses at fixed reference parameter theta=0.

directional_derivative is the right derivative along the supplied (step_direction, parameter_direction), generally nonlinear in direction. The left parameter derivative is the quotient as theta approaches zero from below: it is the negative of the response to direction (0,-1). All fields use volume units per dimensionless step/parameter as applicable.

docs.title: ordinary_parameter_derivative property
docs.text: Scalar theta derivative at fixed step, not joint differentiability.

docs.title: prepare_polyhedral_event_boundary(fixed_cells, moving_cells, velocity, *, max_step, parameter_radius)
docs.text:
Certify two adjacent charts at one supplied event exchange at theta=0.

Cells use one dimensionless affine design parameter, fixed facet normals and fixed translation velocity. Geometry, displacements and velocity share length units; step is dimensionless on [0,max_step]. Positive cell volume, disjoint same-body interiors and initially disjoint cross-body interiors must have strict validity certificates across the returned parameter region.

parameter_radius is a positive exact reference-center choice: prepare regular charts at its negative and positive values. It is not a tolerance, finite-difference increment or claimed domain radius. This function does not discover a boundary or search for suitable centers. Their certified open regions must adjoin at zero, with the same affine event inventory and exactly one isolated pair of distinct event functions meeting inside the path. Other event ties, static feasibility changes, or invalid geometry raise ValueError, even for some physically valid families.

Vertices and displacements denote represented float64 coordinates; centers and queries preserve supplied Fraction values. Rebased cells/planes are exact, without rebuilding rounded center coordinates. Polynomial closures must agree with the fixed-reference geometry. No observations are fitted. This host preparation and its response query are not JAX transformations. Global exact rigid transforms preserve values and responses; scaling all length inputs by s multiplies them by s**3. Independently rounded inputs can change the certificate. The implementation is intended for small cells.

Example::

from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import product
import numpy as np

stock = np.array(list(product((0., 1.), repeat=3)))
cutter = np.array(list(product((-1.5, -.5), (-1., 2.), (-1., 2.))))
shift = np.zeros((1, 8, 3))
shift[0, cutter[:, 0] == -1.5, 0] = -1.
prepared = prepare_polyhedral_event_boundary(
    [AffinePolyhedralCell(stock, np.zeros((1, 8, 3)))],
    [AffinePolyhedralCell(cutter, shift)], (1., 0., 0.),
    max_step=3., parameter_radius=Fraction(1, 8),
)
response = polyhedral_event_boundary_response(prepared, Fraction(3, 2))
assert response.left_parameter_derivative == 1
assert response.right_parameter_derivative == 0

docs.title: specialize_polyhedral_event_boundary(prepared, parameter)
docs.text:
Build the ordinary finite profile at any certified theta, including zero.

Fraction parameters retain their exact values; floats denote their exact binary64 values. Outer domain endpoints reject. The existing profile uses JAX x64 and may reject unresolved float event packing or coefficient range. Its usual target/range queries apply, including empty, singleton and interval target solution sets. No derivative of target selection is added.

docs.title: polyhedral_event_boundary_response(prepared, step, *, step_direction=0, parameter_direction=1)
docs.text:
Return exact one-sided volume responses at (step,theta=0).

Direction means (step,theta)=(step,0)+epsilon*(step_direction, parameter_direction) for epsilon approaching zero from above. Tangent event rays require agreement of all incident polynomial limits; directions exiting the translation interval raise ValueError. The direction map can be nonlinear; this is not a JVP, JAX gradient, or derivative of a root set. No higher derivative or general boundary discovery is provided.

docs.title: Bounded dimension-and-position search
docs.text:
brepax.experimental.polyhedral_design.polyhedral_design_target searches a closed parameter interval inside a prepared event-boundary certificate or an automatically continued domain. It chooses a parameter and translation step that meet the target-volume allowance, while bounding how much the absolute change from an initial parameter could still improve. It does not assume a monotone volume or connected feasible set.

Using boundary from the example above:

from brepax.experimental.polyhedral_design import polyhedral_design_target

result = polyhedral_design_target(
    boundary, 1,
    parameter_bounds=(Fraction(-1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)),
    initial_parameter=Fraction(-1, 8),
    parameter_tolerance=1e-4,
    step_tolerance=1e-10,
    volume_tolerance=1e-8,
    max_boxes=256,
)
if result.witness is not None:
    theta, step = result.witness.parameter, result.witness.step
    # Validate this numerical design and edit against actual rebuilt CAD.

For a supplied event-boundary certificate, the parameter bounds must lie strictly inside its open outer endpoints. For continuation, they must lie inside the requested closed preparation window; unconfirmed parts remain in the objective lower bound. Scalar floats denote exact binary64 inputs; use Fraction when an exact rational target or bound matters. volume_tolerance defines the allowed absolute volume residual. status="optimal_within_tolerance" certifies that the gap between the returned change and the best possible change is at most parameter_tolerance; an unresolved result may have a larger gap or no witness. step_tolerance instead controls numerical target-position refinement.

The returned witness is checked at its actual binary64 parameter and step. Its objective supplies an upper bound; unresolved parameter intervals supply a lower bound. A witness can remain useful when the optimality gap is unresolved. An infeasible result requires excluding the entire requested interval; merely finding no witness is not enough. Exact target reachability is distinct from meeting the volume allowance. Isolated feasible points, numerical packing limits and refinement caps can prevent resolution.

This host operation uses the existing x64 profile specialization and its packing limits; it is not a traced optimizer and supplies no selection gradient. The objective measures distance in the supplied parameter coordinate; rescaling that coordinate also rescales the objective and parameter tolerance. With dimensionless parameter and step, rigid coordinate changes preserve feasibility and optimal objective values. Scaling geometry, affine displacements and velocity by s requires target and volume tolerance to scale by s**3. Exact represented-coordinate laws do not certify separately rounded geometry or the accuracy of an OCCT edit. See the bound derivation.

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.design_search \
  --output /tmp/design-search.json

The bounded comparison searches the design dimension as well as translation. It compares the certified model with complete fixed-profile rebuilding and adaptive CAD observations, with whole-task Boolean and cooperative wall limits. Reports retain proposed model witnesses even when CAD rejects them, independent optimality enclosures, every measured probe, and fresh final Common/Cut checks. The model's optimality certificate and CAD validity are separate findings; sampled baselines do not claim global infeasibility. These constructed tasks are mechanism checks, not evidence of generalization or runtime superiority.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.polyhedral_design
docs.text: Bounded design search over certified polyhedral parameter regions.

docs.title: DesignTargetWitness dataclass
docs.text: An executable binary64 pair, checked in exact represented-model arithmetic.

docs.title: DesignTargetResult dataclass
docs.text:
A bounded search certificate, not a complete design-feasibility atlas.

The lower objective bound concerns continuous real parameter/step pairs in the queried closed domain and volume band. The upper bound belongs to the returned binary64 witness, whose volume and residual are exact rational model values. infeasible excludes the entire continuous domain; unresolved retains regions not excluded within the search budget. No status certifies source CAD, an exact central-target root, or a gradient.

docs.title: optimality_gap property
docs.text: Certified objective gap when an executable witness is available.

docs.title: DesignQueryFailure dataclass
docs.text: A valid exact parameter whose existing numerical profile could not be packed.

docs.title: polyhedral_design_target(prepared, target, *, parameter_bounds, initial_parameter, parameter_tolerance, step_tolerance, volume_tolerance, max_boxes=256, max_refinements=128)
docs.text:
Minimize design change while finding a target-volume translation action.

For a supplied event boundary, search a finite closed parameter interval strictly inside its open certificate. For automatic continuation, search inside its requested closed domain, retaining uncovered regions. The objective is abs(theta-initial_parameter); the constraint is abs(V(step,theta)-target) <= volume_tolerance. This volume tolerance defines a feasible band, unlike the exact-existence semantics of polyhedral_translation_targets. Both returned coordinates are binary64 values, rechecked as exact rationals against the original band and domain.

Parameters and step are dimensionless; target/tolerance have volume units. Scale both by s**3 when scaling geometry, displacements, and velocity by s. Exact coordinate-frame laws and represented-input limitations of the prepared model apply. This host query is neither JAX-transformable nor a derivative of target selection, and retains existing JAX x64/profile packing requirements. Failed numerical packing remains explicitly recorded.

parameter_tolerance is the allowed objective gap for an optimal_within_tolerance result. step_tolerance controls candidate-root refinement, not a separate feasibility constraint. max_boxes caps examined design intervals and isolated points across all charts; max_refinements caps each existing root-isolation path. Initial candidate queries at domain/chart endpoints are additional work, reported by point_queries. Preparation has its own chart/attempt limits. Fixed range tolerances can leave bound floors; isolated feasible points, unavailable float actions, or exhausted budgets may remain unresolved. No finite-completeness guarantee is made.

Every uncovered region, including an isolated boundary point, contributes its distance from the initial parameter to the global objective lower bound. Incomplete coverage can still certify a gap if all uncovered regions are sufficiently far away; it cannot establish global infeasibility. remaining_intervals contains conservative closed envelopes of regions not excluded, including uncovered ones. Exact coverage membership and stop reasons remain on the prepared continuation, separately from this status.

Example::

result = polyhedral_design_target(
    boundary, 0.2, parameter_bounds=(-0.1, 0.1),
    initial_parameter=0.08, parameter_tolerance=1e-4,
    step_tolerance=1e-10, volume_tolerance=1e-8,
)
if result.witness is not None:
    # Independently validate this model action with the actual CAD.
    theta, step = result.witness.parameter, result.witness.step

docs.title: Automatic event continuation
docs.text:
brepax.experimental.polyhedral_continuation starts from an ordinary design parameter and discovers isolated exchanges of translation-event order. It retains the same explicit convex cells, one affine design parameter, fixed facet normals and fixed translation velocity as the local parameter model. It does not require event positions or trial radii from the caller.

Using stock, tool, and changes from the event-boundary example above:

from brepax.experimental.polyhedral_continuation import prepare_polyhedral_continuation

coverage = prepare_polyhedral_continuation(
    [AffinePolyhedralCell(stock, np.zeros((1, 8, 3)))],
    [AffinePolyhedralCell(tool, changes)], (1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    max_step=3,
    parameter_bounds=(Fraction(-1, 4), Fraction(1, 4)),
    seed_parameter=Fraction(-1, 8),
    max_charts=8,
    max_center_trials=8,
)
result = polyhedral_design_target(
    coverage, 1,
    parameter_bounds=coverage.parameter_bounds,
    initial_parameter=Fraction(-1, 8),
    parameter_tolerance=1e-4,
    step_tolerance=1e-10,
    volume_tolerance=1e-8,
)

The original cells at parameter zero must admit fixed-normal preparation, and the seed must admit a regular local chart. A nonregular seed, an unsupported frontier, exhausted chart/refinement budgets, or an event at the requested window endpoint can leave an interval or singleton unconfirmed. This is not a claim that the geometry is invalid or the target unreachable. Preparation retains open chart intervals, separately certified event points, and failure reasons. Exact rational rebasing preserves the original family, including at non-binary event positions; it does not round the shape to create a new family.

The design query uses a single interval budget across the covered regions and retains uncovered regions in its global objective lower bound. A distant unconfirmed region can coexist with optimal_within_tolerance; it cannot be silently dropped to declare whole-window infeasibility. The returned numerical parameter and step are rechecked against the original global model.

Exact volume laws apply on jointly certified inputs, but the current selection of sufficient separating certificates can change the covered region after a coordinate rotation. Coverage, resource-limited status, and the choice among equal-cost numerical edits are not promised to be equivariant. Simultaneous event exchanges, general geometric changes, arbitrary STEP decomposition and gradients of the selected design remain outside this contract. See the continuation argument.

uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.continuation \
  --output /tmp/continuation.json

The comparison uses stepped and oblique geometry mechanisms, with separate unsupported-frontier controls. It supplies no event locations to the automatic method. Reports distinguish the first completed Common observation meeting the volume band, retrospective qualification against the independent design optimum, and fresh final Cut validation. The automatic query finishes before its first CAD observation; no internal candidate is assigned an earlier observation time. Preparation and all attempted operations are charged. These constructed tasks do not establish generalization or a runtime advantage.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.polyhedral_continuation
docs.text: Bounded automatic continuation for one affine polyhedral design parameter.

docs.title: PreparedPolyhedralContinuation dataclass
docs.text:
Covered charts and explicit uncertainty on a closed design window.

A gap is unconfirmed coverage, not invalid geometry or target infeasibility. Boundary parameters are included only after both adjoining chart closures agree with an independently assembled exact fixed-parameter profile.

docs.title: attempts property
docs.text: Every seed, trial center and unresolved frontier observation.

docs.title: boundary_parameters property
docs.text: Automatically discovered and certified isolated exchange parameters.

docs.title: chart_count property
docs.text: Number of accepted regular charts, including the seed when available.

docs.title: uncovered property
docs.text: Unconfirmed portions of the query window, retaining endpoint membership.

docs.title: prepare_polyhedral_continuation(fixed_cells, moving_cells, velocity, *, max_step, parameter_bounds, seed_parameter, max_charts=8, max_center_trials=8)
docs.text:
Discover isolated event exchanges from a regular seed, within a budget.

Supply original float64 vertex cells with one affine, dimensionless design parameter, fixed facet normals and fixed translation velocity. The seed is an ordinary design parameter, not a supplied event or a finite-difference radius. Original cells at theta=0 must admit fixed-normal cell preparation; a nonzero seed does not bypass a nonregular original cell reference. Exact affine guard roots propose frontiers; each accepted transition has one isolated event pair, unchanged event inventory, valid non-event guards and equal exact closures. No rounded rebased vertices are substituted.

The finite closed window must contain the seed. max_charts caps accepted charts including the seed; max_center_trials caps exact rational side centers per frontier. Failed trials remain in attempts. Malformed arrays, nonfinite scalars and invalid bounds/budgets raise ValueError. A family whose seed or next chart cannot be certified instead leaves explicit gaps. No seed search, simultaneous-event handling, or alternative separator search is performed. An event at a window endpoint may remain an uncovered point.

Cell coordinates, displacements and velocity have length units; translation step and parameter are dimensionless. Exact frame changes preserve volume on jointly certified parameters; scaling all lengths by s scales it by s**3. The sufficient separator chosen by existing preparation can depend on the frame: coverage and resolution status are not promised equivariant. Rounded input, source CAD and geometric invalidity are not certified. This host preparation has no JAX transformation or completeness guarantee; specialization retains existing JAX x64 and numerical packing requirements.

Example::

prepared = prepare_polyhedral_continuation(
    fixed_cells, moving_cells, (1, 0, 0), max_step=4,
    parameter_bounds=(-0.05, 0.6), seed_parameter=0,
)
if not prepared.uncovered:
    path = specialize_polyhedral_continuation(prepared, 0.5)
    # Existing exact target/range queries apply to this model path.

docs.title: specialize_polyhedral_continuation(prepared, parameter)
docs.text:
Specialize only a certified parameter; unresolved coverage raises ValueError.

Fraction values retain the original affine family exactly. Existing translation-profile packing may reject unresolved float64 event chambers or coefficient scales even when the host parameter is certified.

docs.title: Selecting finite edits with a CAD budget
docs.text:
uv run --group benchmark python -m benchmarks.multi_contact.selection \
  --output /tmp/finite-selection.json

This benchmark compares analytical candidate ordering and CAD confirmation with CAD-only adaptive selection. Its separate amount-refinement panel uses bounded proposals and only returns observed actions. It promises neither monotonic volume along arbitrary motion nor target reachability. A negative error difference relative to the fixed candidate grid is possible when a refined amount improves on every grid action.

Fresh synthetic geometry groups and five grouped train/test partitions keep calibration apart from each evaluated shape; repeated targets are not independent shapes. Reports retain failed or unsupported inputs and targets exceeding a known total-material bound. Probe attempts and final independent Common/Cut checks have separate costs. Cached replay timings do not establish end-to-end speed superiority. The experimental comparison is not a general optimizer API or evidence for arbitrary STEP inputs.

docs.title: brepax.experimental.applications.mold_direction
docs.text:
Mold pull-direction optimization via differentiable undercut analysis.

Given a shape defined by its SDF, estimates the volume of material that would prevent mold removal in a given pull direction. The undercut criterion is SDF-based: a surface point is undercut when its outward normal opposes the pull direction (dot(normal, direction) < 0).

Both the undercut volume and the optimization loop are fully differentiable, enabling gradient-based search over the unit sphere S^2.

docs.title: MoldDirectionResult dataclass
docs.text:
Result of mold direction optimization.

Attributes:

Name Type Description direction Float[Array, 3]

Optimized pull direction (unit vector).

trajectory Float[Array, 'n 3']

Direction at each step, shape (steps+1, 3).

losses list[float]

Undercut volume at each step.

converged bool

Whether loss change dropped below tolerance.

docs.title: optimize_mold_direction(shape_sdf, initial_direction, *, lo, hi, resolution=64, steps=100, lr=0.01, tol=1e-06)
docs.text:
Find the mold pull direction that minimizes undercut volume.

Uses projected gradient descent on S^2: after each gradient step the direction vector is re-normalized to the unit sphere.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default shape_sdf Callable[[Float[Array, 3]], Float[Array, '']]

Signed distance function for a single query point.

required initial_direction Float[Array, 3]

Starting pull direction (will be normalized).

required lo Float[Array, 3]

Lower corner of the evaluation domain.

required hi Float[Array, 3]

Upper corner of the evaluation domain.

required resolution int

Grid resolution per axis.

64 steps int

Maximum optimization steps.

100 lr float

Learning rate for gradient descent.

0.01 tol float

Convergence tolerance on absolute loss change.

1e-06

Returns:

Type Description MoldDirectionResult

MoldDirectionResult with optimized direction and diagnostics.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> from brepax.primitives import Box
>>> box = Box(
...     center=jnp.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
...     half_extents=jnp.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.5]),
... )
>>> result = optimize_mold_direction(
...     box.sdf,
...     jnp.array([1.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
...     lo=jnp.array([-2.0, -2.0, -2.0]),
...     hi=jnp.array([2.0, 2.0, 2.0]),
...     resolution=32,
...     steps=50,
... )

docs.title: undercut_volume(shape_sdf, direction, *, lo, hi, resolution=64)
docs.text:
Estimate undercut volume for a mold pull direction.

Undercut is defined as the set of interior points whose SDF spatial gradient (outward normal) opposes the pull direction. Both the interior membership and the undercut condition are smoothed with sigmoid indicators scaled by the grid cell width, ensuring the estimate improves with resolution.

Normals are estimated via central finite differences to avoid NaN gradients at degenerate SDF points (cylinder axis, box center, etc.).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default shape_sdf Callable[[Float[Array, 3]], Float[Array, '']]

Signed distance function for a single query point. Must accept shape (3,) and return scalar.

required direction Float[Array, 3]

Unit pull direction on S^2.

required lo Float[Array, 3]

Lower corner of the evaluation domain.

required hi Float[Array, 3]

Upper corner of the evaluation domain.

required resolution int

Grid resolution per axis.

64

Returns:

Type Description Float[Array, '']

Scalar estimated undercut volume.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> from brepax.primitives import Box
>>> box = Box(
...     center=jnp.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
...     half_extents=jnp.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.5]),
... )
>>> vol = undercut_volume(
...     box.sdf,
...     jnp.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]),
...     lo=jnp.array([-2.0, -2.0, -2.0]),
...     hi=jnp.array([2.0, 2.0, 2.0]),
...     resolution=32,
... )

docs.title: brepax.experimental.applications.cad_frame.CadFrame dataclass
docs.text:
Fixed host metadata with x_external = origin + length_scale * x_work.

length_scale is external length units per working length unit. Choose it once from a reference design size, before constructing CAD, and keep it fixed throughout editing. For a 40 mm reference expressed in metres, use length_scale=0.001 to work at size 40. origin is in external units. Directions/rotations are unchanged by this positive uniform scale; any rigid rotation belongs to the supplied geometry model.

Array conversions support JIT, vmap and differentiation when this frame is captured as fixed metadata. A degree-k scalar scales by sk and its gradient with respect to external lengths by s(k-1). The frame itself is not a differentiable model. Prefer x64 for CAD accuracy.

Normalize design dimensions and dimensional meshing/smoothing tolerances BEFORE OCCT construction. This does not infer STEP units, repair existing B-Reps, or guarantee CAD accuracy at arbitrary scales. Output transforms retain OCCT's tolerance semantics; they do not tighten tolerances.

Example

import jax import jax.numpy as jnp frame = CadFrame(0.001, (1.0, 2.0, 3.0)) def sphere_volume(radius): ... r = frame.working_lengths(radius) ... return frame.external_measure(4 * jnp.pi * r**3 / 3, 3) derivative = jax.jit(jax.grad(sphere_volume))(jnp.array(0.003))

docs.text: Restore a length, area or volume; JAX propagates the unit chain rule.

docs.text: Restore point positions; evaluate scalar metrics before this step.

docs.title: restore_shape(working_shape)
docs.text:
Copy a working B-Rep into external coordinates on the host.

Does not copy triangulations. Raises ValueError for null input and RuntimeError if OCCT returns an invalid result. This is an output conversion, not a traced operation or a mesh-to-CAD reconstruction.

docs.text: Convert external lengths (including deflections) to working units.

docs.title: Integration benchmark report
docs.text:
A reproducible measurement of BRepAX's volume paths and face-level metric coverage on the project's standard STEP fixture set.

The report below is a checked-in measurement snapshot. Building the docs includes it without rerunning the benchmark, so its results need not describe the current source revision. Its update history is available in Git history. Regenerate it on the revision being evaluated with:

uv run python -m benchmarks.integration_report.run_benchmark

docs.title: What this report does not claim
docs.text:
• No "first" or "unique" claim about any BRepAX path.
  • No quantitative speed comparison against external systems.
  • No claim that BRepAX outperforms any external system on tasks those systems were designed for.

The competitor landscape section below is qualitative feature coverage only, not a numerical head-to-head; cells are marked "hypothesis" where they reflect best-effort reading of public documentation.

docs.title: BRepAX Integration Benchmark Report
docs.text:
Reproducible measurement of the BRepAX volume paths and face-level metric coverage on the project's standard STEP fixture set.

This report is the output of one benchmark command — uv run python -m benchmarks.integration_report.run_benchmark. No claim of novelty is made beyond what the tables below directly show. Comparisons against external systems (Manifold, PyTorch3D, JAX-FEM) are qualitative; see competitor_landscape.md for the framing and its limitations.

Volume paths use a sigmoid grid integration at resolution=32 (per-axis cell count); the mesh divergence path uses the OCCT BRepMesh tessellation at the default deflection. OCCT BRepGProp is the reference and is computed analytically on the exact B-Rep, not on the mesh.

How to read this table.

  • divergence is the mesh divergence-theorem volume (Stokes' theorem on the BRepMesh tessellation). Differentiable through triangle vertex positions. Strongest production path.
  • mesh_sdf is the mesh-based signed distance field (unsigned distance to the nearest triangle, signed by generalized winding number) integrated with a sigmoid indicator on the same grid as the CSG paths. Differentiable through triangle vertex positions and the sigmoid integrator.
  • gwn is the generalized-winding-number indicator integrated directly: sigmoid((wn - 0.5) * GWN_SHARPNESS) summed over the grid. Sharpness is fixed at module level (the field is dimensionless 0..1, so the cell-width-based sharpness used by the SDF integrators is not appropriate here). This single fixed configuration is one operating point; sweeping sharpness / resolution / mesh deflection is out of scope for this PR.
  • CSG-Stump is the analytical primitive DNF, integrated with a sigmoid indicator. Differentiable through primitive parameters. Bounded by the BSpline half-space limitation (see project_bspline_halfspace.md in memory; concretely the CSG-Stump DNF cannot consume a finite trimmed BSpline patch as a half-space ingredient — ADR-0019, ADR-0020).
  • TrimmedCSGStump carries per-face trim metadata for standalone trimmed-face SDF queries; on the DNF path it is bit-equivalent to DifferentiableCSGStump per ADR-0019 / ADR-0020. Equality of the csg and trim columns is the expected outcome.

docs.title: Qualitative competitor landscape
docs.text:
Important caveat. This is a qualitative feature-coverage table, not a head-to-head numerical benchmark. Numerical comparison would require running the same problem (e.g. volume of a Linkrods-class trimmed-BSpline shape with derivatives w.r.t. control points) through each system, which none of the listed competitors are directly designed to express. The table reports what each system is built to do, not who is faster on a shared benchmark. Cells marked "hypothesis" are best-effort observations from public documentation; treat them as starting points, not citations.

System / Path STEP / B-Rep input Per-face awareness Trimmed BSpline Differentiable volume Per-face metrics Notes BRepAX divergence_volume yes (via OCCT) derived from face triangulation via OCCT BRepMesh yes — through triangle vertex positions yes (this PR's coverage table) strongest production path on this report BRepAX evaluate_stump_volume yes (via OCCT + reconstruction) primitive-based weak (ADR-0020: BSpline patches are not a CSG-Stump DNF half-space ingredient) yes — through primitive parameters not directly analytical-dominant fixtures BRepAX TrimmedCSGStump.volume yes per-face trim metadata stored metadata stored, not on DNF SDF path (ADR-0019, ADR-0020) yes — through primitive parameters not directly bit-equivalent to evaluate_stump_volume on the DNF path Manifold (manifold3d) indirect (mesh only) mesh-level no (mesh) no (Boolean is exact, not differentiable) no hypothesis: robust mesh boolean, not a CAD-differentiable kernel PyTorch3D mesh ops no (mesh only) mesh-level no (mesh) partial (mesh deformations are differentiable) no hypothesis: differentiable mesh operations, not B-Rep JAX-FEM no (FE mesh) element-level no (mesh) yes — but for FE objectives, not CAD volume no hypothesis: physics solver, not a CAD geometry kernel

The framing BRepAX is built around — gradients flow from STEP / B-Rep through to a JAX scalar — does not have an obvious head-to-head counterpart in the listed systems, because they enter the pipeline at a different stage (mesh, or FE mesh). This is the BRepAX position to test, not assume; the right way to falsify it is to run a published benchmark that asks each system to solve the same B-Rep-rooted optimisation problem. No such benchmark is bundled with this PR.

What is not claimed by this report:

  • No "first" or "unique" claim about any BRepAX path. Other research projects exist on differentiable B-Rep, signed distance functions on trimmed surfaces, and topology-aware boolean differentiation; this report does not survey them.
  • No quantitative speed comparison against any external system.
  • No claim that BRepAX outperforms any competitor on tasks they were designed for. Manifold's exact mesh boolean and JAX-FEM's PDE solver are not in scope here.

What this report does assert:

  • The numbers in volume accuracy and face-level metric coverage are reproducible from the bundled command on the bundled fixtures.
  • The CSG-Stump and TrimmedCSGStump rows being equal is consistent with the negative-result ADRs (ADR-0019, ADR-0020).
  • Per-face metric NaN counts on cone / torus / BSpline faces in mean_curvature_per_face are the documented analytical-handler deferral, not failures.

docs.text:
• This is not a new result. The within-stratum precision gap between Method C and Method A is documented in ADR-0009 / ADR-0011 and exercised by the test cited above. This page just surfaces it alongside the rest of the documentation.
  • No claim that Method A is "wrong". The residual it leaves is a documented bias property of the sigmoid-temperature smoothed objective at finite beta.

docs.title: Method-C applied convergence demo
docs.text:
Two disks, C1 = (0, 0), R1 optimised toward the analytical ground truth r1* = 1.5, C2 = (1, 0), R2 = 1. The objective is loss(r1) = (union_area(a, b) - target)^2 with the target computed in closed form by brepax.analytical.disk_disk.disk_disk_union_area. The same gradient-descent loop runs twice, once with method="stratum" (Method C) and once with method="smoothing", k=0.1, beta=0.1, resolution=128 (Method A). The numbers below are the output of one command.

Settings: lr=0.01, max_steps=200, init_r1=0.8, target_area=7.880057 (closed form).

docs.title: Final-step numbers
docs.text:
Method final r1 pos err final loss steps Method C (stratum) 1.501310 1.31e-03 3.62e-06 200 Method A (smoothing, beta=0.1) 1.478751 2.12e-02 1.75e-15 200

Method C converges to the grid-discretisation floor of its stratum-aware integrator. Method A's residual is the bias introduced by the sigmoid temperature beta; it does not shrink with more gradient-descent steps because the bias is inherent to the smoothed objective, not a transient of the optimiser. This is the documented behaviour from tests/benchmarks/test_optimization_trajectory.py; the purpose of this page is to make it visible alongside the rest of the documentation rather than to claim it as a new result.

docs.title: BSplineSurface
docs.text:
Bases: Primitive

B-spline surface defined by a control point grid and knot vectors.

The SDF is computed via closest-point projection onto the surface. Control points are differentiable design variables: jax.grad flows through the unrolled Newton projection.

Attributes:

Name Type Description control_points Float[Array, 'nu nv 3']

Control point grid, shape (n_u, n_v, 3).

knots_u Array

Knot vector in u-direction.

knots_v Array

Knot vector in v-direction.

degree_u int

Polynomial degree in u.

degree_v int

Polynomial degree in v.

Examples:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> pts = jnp.array([[[0,0,0],[1,0,0]],
...                  [[0,1,0],[1,1,0]]], dtype=float)
>>> knots = jnp.array([0., 0., 1., 1.])
>>> surf = BSplineSurface(
...     control_points=pts, knots_u=knots, knots_v=knots,
...     degree_u=1, degree_v=1,
... )
>>> d = surf.sdf(jnp.array([0.5, 0.5, 1.0]))
Source code in src/brepax/primitives/bspline_surface.py 
class BSplineSurface(Primitive):
    """B-spline surface defined by a control point grid and knot vectors.

    The SDF is computed via closest-point projection onto the surface.
    Control points are differentiable design variables: ``jax.grad``
    flows through the unrolled Newton projection.

    Attributes:
        control_points: Control point grid, shape ``(n_u, n_v, 3)``.
        knots_u: Knot vector in u-direction.
        knots_v: Knot vector in v-direction.
        degree_u: Polynomial degree in u.
        degree_v: Polynomial degree in v.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> pts = jnp.array([[[0,0,0],[1,0,0]],
        ...                  [[0,1,0],[1,1,0]]], dtype=float)
        >>> knots = jnp.array([0., 0., 1., 1.])
        >>> surf = BSplineSurface(
        ...     control_points=pts, knots_u=knots, knots_v=knots,
        ...     degree_u=1, degree_v=1,
        ... )
        >>> d = surf.sdf(jnp.array([0.5, 0.5, 1.0]))
    """

    control_points: Float[Array, "nu nv 3"]
    knots_u: Array = eqx.field()
    knots_v: Array = eqx.field()
    degree_u: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    degree_v: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    weights: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    sign_flip: float = eqx.field(default=1.0, static=True)
    param_u_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    param_v_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    coarse_positions: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    coarse_normals: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_polygon: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_mask: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the B-spline surface.

        For batched inputs, each point is projected independently via
        Newton iteration.
        """
        shape = x.shape[:-1]
        flat = x.reshape(-1, 3)

        # Coarse grid sampling: compute once, reuse for all query points
        from brepax.nurbs.projection import _COARSE_GRID

        u_lo = self.knots_u[self.degree_u]
        u_hi = self.knots_u[-self.degree_u - 1]
        v_lo = self.knots_v[self.degree_v]
        v_hi = self.knots_v[-self.degree_v - 1]
        us = jnp.linspace(u_lo, u_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        vs = jnp.linspace(v_lo, v_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        u_grid, v_grid = jnp.meshgrid(us, vs, indexing="ij")
        u_flat_g = u_grid.ravel()
        v_flat_g = v_grid.ravel()

        def _eval_sample(u: Array, v: Array) -> Array:
            return evaluate_surface(
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u,
                v,
                self.weights,
            )

        samples = jax.vmap(_eval_sample)(u_flat_g, v_flat_g)

        def _single_sdf(q: Array) -> Array:
            # Find closest coarse sample (stop_gradient: argmin is non-diff)
            dists = jnp.sum((samples - q) ** 2, axis=-1)
            best = jnp.argmin(dists)
            u0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(u_flat_g[best])
            v0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(v_flat_g[best])
            return bspline_sdf(
                q,
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u0=u0,
                v0=v0,
                weights=self.weights,
                param_u_range=self.param_u_range,
                param_v_range=self.param_v_range,
                sign_flip=self.sign_flip,
                coarse_positions=self.coarse_positions,
                coarse_normals=self.coarse_normals,
            )

        result = jax.vmap(_single_sdf)(flat)
        return result.reshape(shape)

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        params: dict[str, Array] = {
            "control_points": self.control_points,
            "knots_u": self.knots_u,
            "knots_v": self.knots_v,
        }
        if self.weights is not None:
            params["weights"] = self.weights
        return params

An axis-aligned box defined by center and half-extents.

Attributes:

Source code in src/brepax/primitives/box.py 
class Box(Primitive):
    """An axis-aligned box defined by center and half-extents.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the box (3,).
        half_extents: Half-size in each dimension (3,).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    half_extents: Float[Array, "3"]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the box surface."""
        q = jnp.abs(x - self.center) - self.half_extents
        qp = jnp.maximum(q, 0.0)
        # eps avoids NaN gradient from norm at zero (same pattern as FiniteCylinder)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(qp**2, axis=-1) + 1e-20)
        is_outside = jnp.max(q, axis=-1) > 0
        outside = jnp.where(is_outside, outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.max(q, axis=-1), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"center": self.center, "half_extents": self.half_extents}

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Box volume: 8 * hx * hy * hz."""
        return 8.0 * jnp.prod(self.half_extents)

class Cone(Primitive):
    """An infinite cone defined by apex position, axis direction, and half-angle.

    The cone extends infinitely from the apex along the axis direction.
    The SDF is positive outside, negative inside.

    Attributes:
        apex: Apex point of the cone (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector from apex (3,). Must be normalized.
        angle: Half-angle in radians (0, pi/2).
    """

    apex: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    angle: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cone surface."""
        v = x - self.apex
        # Distance along axis
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2, 1e-20))
        sin_a = jnp.sin(self.angle)
        cos_a = jnp.cos(self.angle)
        # Signed distance: positive outside cone, negative inside
        return jnp.where(
            h >= 0,
            perp * cos_a - h * sin_a,
            jnp.sqrt(perp**2 + h**2),
        )

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"apex": self.apex, "axis": self.axis, "angle": self.angle}

class Cylinder(Primitive):
    """An infinite cylinder defined by a point on the axis, axis direction, and radius.

    The SDF measures perpendicular distance from the axis line minus the radius.
    The cylinder extends infinitely along the axis direction.

    Attributes:
        point: A point on the cylinder axis (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Scalar radius (must be positive).
    """

    point: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cylinder surface.

        Computes the perpendicular distance from each query point to
        the cylinder axis, then subtracts the radius.
        """
        # Vector from axis point to query
        v = x - self.point
        # Project onto axis to get parallel component
        proj_len = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        # Perpendicular component
        perp = v - proj_len * self.axis
        perp_dist = jnp.linalg.norm(perp, axis=-1)
        return perp_dist - self.radius  # type: ignore[no-any-return]

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"point": self.point, "axis": self.axis, "radius": self.radius}

class FiniteCylinder(Primitive):
    """A finite cylinder (capped) defined by center, axis, radius, and height.

    The cylinder is centered at `center` and extends `height/2` in each
    direction along `axis`.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the cylinder (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Cylinder radius (must be positive).
        height: Total height along the axis (must be positive).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]
    height: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the finite cylinder surface."""
        v = x - self.center
        # Axial distance from center
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(perp_sq, 1e-20))

        # Signed distances to the two constraints
        d_radial = perp - self.radius
        d_axial = jnp.abs(h) - self.height / 2.0

        # SDF of intersection of infinite cylinder and slab.
        # Use sqrt with eps to avoid NaN gradient at [0, 0].
        dr = jnp.maximum(d_radial, 0.0)
        da = jnp.maximum(d_axial, 0.0)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(dr**2 + da**2 + 1e-20)
        # Subtract the eps contribution when truly outside
        outside = jnp.where((dr > 0) | (da > 0), outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.maximum(d_radial, d_axial), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {
            "center": self.center,
            "axis": self.axis,
            "radius": self.radius,
            "height": self.height,
        }

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Finite cylinder volume: pi * r^2 * h."""
        return jnp.pi * self.radius**2 * self.height

class Primitive(eqx.Module):
    """Base class for all geometric primitives.

    Each primitive exposes an SDF, gradient w.r.t. spatial coordinates,
    and a list of design parameters that gradients can flow into.
    """

    @abstractmethod
    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... dim"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Evaluate the signed distance function at query points."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Analytical volume of this primitive.

        Returns the finite volume for bounded primitives (Sphere, Box, etc.).
        Unbounded primitives (Cylinder, Plane, Cone) return inf.
        Override in subclasses with known analytical formulas.
        Differentiable via jax.grad for gradient computation.
        """
        # Default: unbounded primitive has infinite volume
        import jax.numpy as jnp

        return jnp.array(jnp.inf)

class Torus(Primitive):
    """A torus defined by center, axis, major radius, and minor radius.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the torus (3,).
        axis: Unit normal to the torus plane (3,). Must be normalized.
        major_radius: Distance from center to tube center.
        minor_radius: Tube radius.
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    major_radius: Float[Array, ""]
    minor_radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the torus surface."""
        v = x - self.center
        # Component along axis (height above torus plane)
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Component in the torus plane (distance from center axis)
        v_plane_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
        v_plane = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(v_plane_sq, 1e-20))
        # Distance from the tube center ring
        q = jnp.sqrt((v_plane - self.major_radius) ** 2 + h**2)
        return q - self.minor_radius

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {
            "center": self.center,
            "major_radius": self.major_radius,
            "minor_radius": self.minor_radius,
        }

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Torus volume: 2 * pi^2 * R * r^2."""
        return 2.0 * jnp.pi**2 * self.major_radius * self.minor_radius**2

class Box(Primitive):
    """An axis-aligned box defined by center and half-extents.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the box (3,).
        half_extents: Half-size in each dimension (3,).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    half_extents: Float[Array, "3"]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the box surface."""
        q = jnp.abs(x - self.center) - self.half_extents
        qp = jnp.maximum(q, 0.0)
        # eps avoids NaN gradient from norm at zero (same pattern as FiniteCylinder)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(qp**2, axis=-1) + 1e-20)
        is_outside = jnp.max(q, axis=-1) > 0
        outside = jnp.where(is_outside, outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.max(q, axis=-1), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"center": self.center, "half_extents": self.half_extents}

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Box volume: 8 * hx * hy * hz."""
        return 8.0 * jnp.prod(self.half_extents)

docs.text:
B-spline surface primitive with differentiable SDF.

Wraps the NURBS evaluation and closest-point projection pipeline as a :class:~brepax.primitives.Primitive so that existing Boolean operations and metrics work with NURBS surfaces automatically.

The surface is unbounded (a single open patch, not a closed solid), so volume() returns infinity and Boolean operations fall back to grid-based evaluation, matching the pattern used by :class:~brepax.primitives.Plane and :class:~brepax.primitives.Cylinder.

class BSplineSurface(Primitive):
    """B-spline surface defined by a control point grid and knot vectors.

    The SDF is computed via closest-point projection onto the surface.
    Control points are differentiable design variables: ``jax.grad``
    flows through the unrolled Newton projection.

    Attributes:
        control_points: Control point grid, shape ``(n_u, n_v, 3)``.
        knots_u: Knot vector in u-direction.
        knots_v: Knot vector in v-direction.
        degree_u: Polynomial degree in u.
        degree_v: Polynomial degree in v.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> pts = jnp.array([[[0,0,0],[1,0,0]],
        ...                  [[0,1,0],[1,1,0]]], dtype=float)
        >>> knots = jnp.array([0., 0., 1., 1.])
        >>> surf = BSplineSurface(
        ...     control_points=pts, knots_u=knots, knots_v=knots,
        ...     degree_u=1, degree_v=1,
        ... )
        >>> d = surf.sdf(jnp.array([0.5, 0.5, 1.0]))
    """

    control_points: Float[Array, "nu nv 3"]
    knots_u: Array = eqx.field()
    knots_v: Array = eqx.field()
    degree_u: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    degree_v: int = eqx.field(static=True)
    weights: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    sign_flip: float = eqx.field(default=1.0, static=True)
    param_u_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    param_v_range: tuple[float, float] | None = eqx.field(default=None, static=True)
    coarse_positions: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    coarse_normals: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_polygon: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)
    trim_mask: Array | None = eqx.field(default=None)

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the B-spline surface.

        For batched inputs, each point is projected independently via
        Newton iteration.
        """
        shape = x.shape[:-1]
        flat = x.reshape(-1, 3)

        # Coarse grid sampling: compute once, reuse for all query points
        from brepax.nurbs.projection import _COARSE_GRID

        u_lo = self.knots_u[self.degree_u]
        u_hi = self.knots_u[-self.degree_u - 1]
        v_lo = self.knots_v[self.degree_v]
        v_hi = self.knots_v[-self.degree_v - 1]
        us = jnp.linspace(u_lo, u_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        vs = jnp.linspace(v_lo, v_hi, _COARSE_GRID)
        u_grid, v_grid = jnp.meshgrid(us, vs, indexing="ij")
        u_flat_g = u_grid.ravel()
        v_flat_g = v_grid.ravel()

        def _eval_sample(u: Array, v: Array) -> Array:
            return evaluate_surface(
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u,
                v,
                self.weights,
            )

        samples = jax.vmap(_eval_sample)(u_flat_g, v_flat_g)

        def _single_sdf(q: Array) -> Array:
            # Find closest coarse sample (stop_gradient: argmin is non-diff)
            dists = jnp.sum((samples - q) ** 2, axis=-1)
            best = jnp.argmin(dists)
            u0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(u_flat_g[best])
            v0 = jax.lax.stop_gradient(v_flat_g[best])
            return bspline_sdf(
                q,
                self.control_points,
                self.knots_u,
                self.knots_v,
                self.degree_u,
                self.degree_v,
                u0=u0,
                v0=v0,
                weights=self.weights,
                param_u_range=self.param_u_range,
                param_v_range=self.param_v_range,
                sign_flip=self.sign_flip,
                coarse_positions=self.coarse_positions,
                coarse_normals=self.coarse_normals,
            )

        result = jax.vmap(_single_sdf)(flat)
        return result.reshape(shape)

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        params: dict[str, Array] = {
            "control_points": self.control_points,
            "knots_u": self.knots_u,
            "knots_v": self.knots_v,
        }
        if self.weights is not None:
            params["weights"] = self.weights
        return params

class Cone(Primitive):
    """An infinite cone defined by apex position, axis direction, and half-angle.

    The cone extends infinitely from the apex along the axis direction.
    The SDF is positive outside, negative inside.

    Attributes:
        apex: Apex point of the cone (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector from apex (3,). Must be normalized.
        angle: Half-angle in radians (0, pi/2).
    """

    apex: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    angle: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cone surface."""
        v = x - self.apex
        # Distance along axis
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2, 1e-20))
        sin_a = jnp.sin(self.angle)
        cos_a = jnp.cos(self.angle)
        # Signed distance: positive outside cone, negative inside
        return jnp.where(
            h >= 0,
            perp * cos_a - h * sin_a,
            jnp.sqrt(perp**2 + h**2),
        )

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"apex": self.apex, "axis": self.axis, "angle": self.angle}

class Cylinder(Primitive):
    """An infinite cylinder defined by a point on the axis, axis direction, and radius.

    The SDF measures perpendicular distance from the axis line minus the radius.
    The cylinder extends infinitely along the axis direction.

    Attributes:
        point: A point on the cylinder axis (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Scalar radius (must be positive).
    """

    point: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the cylinder surface.

        Computes the perpendicular distance from each query point to
        the cylinder axis, then subtracts the radius.
        """
        # Vector from axis point to query
        v = x - self.point
        # Project onto axis to get parallel component
        proj_len = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        # Perpendicular component
        perp = v - proj_len * self.axis
        perp_dist = jnp.linalg.norm(perp, axis=-1)
        return perp_dist - self.radius  # type: ignore[no-any-return]

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"point": self.point, "axis": self.axis, "radius": self.radius}

class FiniteCylinder(Primitive):
    """A finite cylinder (capped) defined by center, axis, radius, and height.

    The cylinder is centered at `center` and extends `height/2` in each
    direction along `axis`.

    Attributes:
        center: Center of the cylinder (3,).
        axis: Unit direction vector of the axis (3,). Must be normalized.
        radius: Cylinder radius (must be positive).
        height: Total height along the axis (must be positive).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    axis: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]
    height: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the finite cylinder surface."""
        v = x - self.center
        # Axial distance from center
        h = jnp.sum(v * self.axis, axis=-1)
        # Perpendicular distance from axis
        perp_sq = jnp.sum(v * v, axis=-1) - h**2
        perp = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(perp_sq, 1e-20))

        # Signed distances to the two constraints
        d_radial = perp - self.radius
        d_axial = jnp.abs(h) - self.height / 2.0

        # SDF of intersection of infinite cylinder and slab.
        # Use sqrt with eps to avoid NaN gradient at [0, 0].
        dr = jnp.maximum(d_radial, 0.0)
        da = jnp.maximum(d_axial, 0.0)
        outside = jnp.sqrt(dr**2 + da**2 + 1e-20)
        # Subtract the eps contribution when truly outside
        outside = jnp.where((dr > 0) | (da > 0), outside, 0.0)
        inside = jnp.minimum(jnp.maximum(d_radial, d_axial), 0.0)
        return outside + inside

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {
            "center": self.center,
            "axis": self.axis,
            "radius": self.radius,
            "height": self.height,
        }

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Finite cylinder volume: pi * r^2 * h."""
        return jnp.pi * self.radius**2 * self.height

docs.title: foot
docs.text:
Analytical foot-of-perpendicular on primitive surfaces.

Each function returns the closest point on an infinite analytical surface (plane, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus) to a query point. Closed form given the primitive parameters; fully differentiable w.r.t. both the query and the primitive parameters.

Scope is the untrimmed surface only; trim-boundary interaction is layered on via Marschner composition in a separate module. Cone and torus inner-region degeneracies (apex, tube axis) are handled with an epsilon guard on the radial direction.

Zero-denominator handling uses a safe-square-then-sqrt pattern that keeps both forward and gradient finite at the degenerate boundary. jnp.linalg.norm(v) has infinite derivative at v = 0; since jnp.where evaluates both branches in the VJP, a naive guard on norm still leaks NaN into jax.grad. The pattern used here switches on the squared norm before sqrt, so the sqrt argument is bounded below by 1 when the query is degenerate:

sq = sum(v * v)
is_ok = sq > eps_sq
safe_sq = where(is_ok, sq, 1.0)
norm = sqrt(safe_sq)   # always >= 1 at the degenerate point
direction = where(is_ok, v / norm, fallback)

docs.title: foot_on_cone(query, apex, axis, angle)
docs.text:
Closest point on the half-cone extending forward of apex.

The cone is the surface r(h) = h * tan(angle) for h >= 0 along axis. For queries that project to h < 0 the foot is clamped to apex.

Source code in src/brepax/primitives/foot.py 
def foot_on_cone(
    query: Float[Array, 3],
    apex: Float[Array, 3],
    axis: Float[Array, 3],
    angle: Float[Array, ""],
) -> Float[Array, 3]:
    """Closest point on the half-cone extending forward of ``apex``.

    The cone is the surface ``r(h) = h * tan(angle)`` for ``h >= 0``
    along ``axis``.  For queries that project to ``h < 0`` the foot is
    clamped to ``apex``.
    """
    v = query - apex
    h = jnp.dot(v, axis)
    radial = v - h * axis
    radial_norm, radial_dir = _safe_unit(radial, _axis_orthogonal(axis))
    cos_a = jnp.cos(angle)
    sin_a = jnp.sin(angle)
    t = h * cos_a + radial_norm * sin_a
    t = jnp.maximum(t, 0.0)
    return apex + t * (cos_a * axis + sin_a * radial_dir)

def foot_on_cylinder(
    query: Float[Array, 3],
    point: Float[Array, 3],
    axis: Float[Array, 3],
    radius: Float[Array, ""],
) -> Float[Array, 3]:
    """Closest point on an infinite cylinder of ``radius`` about the axis.

    On the axis itself the radial direction is ill-defined; a canonical
    unit vector orthogonal to ``axis`` is used to keep the computation
    differentiable.
    """
    v = query - point
    axial_len = jnp.dot(v, axis)
    radial = v - axial_len * axis
    _, direction = _safe_unit(radial, _axis_orthogonal(axis))
    return point + axial_len * axis + radius * direction

def foot_on_sphere(
    query: Float[Array, 3],
    center: Float[Array, 3],
    radius: Float[Array, ""],
) -> Float[Array, 3]:
    """Closest point on a sphere of ``radius`` around ``center``.

    At the center (degenerate) the result is ``center + radius * e_z``;
    an arbitrary direction is required to keep the gradient finite.

    v = query - center
    _, direction = _safe_unit(v, jnp.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))
    return center + radius * direction

    minor_radius: Float[Array, ""],
) -> Float[Array, 3]:
    """Closest point on the torus tube around the major ring.

    Project to the tube-center ring first, then shift outward by
    ``minor_radius``.  On the central axis (``radial == 0``) a canonical
    in-plane direction is used; on the tube center itself
    (``dq == 0``) the fallback is the radial direction.
    """
    v = query - center
    h = jnp.dot(v, axis)
    radial = v - h * axis
    _, radial_dir = _safe_unit(radial, _axis_orthogonal(axis))
    tube_center = center + major_radius * radial_dir
    dq = query - tube_center
    _, dq_dir = _safe_unit(dq, radial_dir)
    return tube_center + minor_radius * dq_dir

class Plane(Primitive):
    """An infinite plane (half-space boundary) defined by normal and offset.

    The SDF is positive on the side the normal points toward (outside),
    and negative on the opposite side (inside).

    Attributes:
        normal: Unit normal vector (3,). Must be normalized.
        offset: Signed distance from origin to the plane along the normal.
    """

    normal: Float[Array, "3"]
    offset: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the plane."""
        return jnp.sum(x * self.normal, axis=-1) - self.offset

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"normal": self.normal, "offset": self.offset}

class Sphere(Primitive):
    """A 3D sphere defined by center and radius.

    Attributes:
        center: Center coordinates (3,).
        radius: Scalar radius (must be positive).
    """

    center: Float[Array, "3"]
    radius: Float[Array, ""]

    def sdf(self, x: Float[Array, "... 3"]) -> Float[Array, "..."]:
        """Signed distance from query points to the sphere surface."""
        return jnp.linalg.norm(x - self.center, axis=-1) - self.radius  # type: ignore[no-any-return]

    def parameters(self) -> dict[str, Array]:
        """Return differentiable design parameters."""
        return {"center": self.center, "radius": self.radius}

    def volume(self) -> Float[Array, ""]:
        """Sphere volume: 4/3 * pi * r^3."""
        return (4.0 / 3.0) * jnp.pi * self.radius**3
